title: VP, Engineering
description: We are hiring a VP of Engineering for a leading technology marketplace being relaunched under new ownership. The platform now processes hundreds of millions of API calls a day and simplifies how millions of developers discover, test, and pay for thousands of public APIs: a single key, a single bill, in-browser testing, code snippets in every major language, across categories from data and sports to communications and AI. It is rare for a developer platform to earn its scale by genuinely removing friction. Your role is full technical ownership of a live system at scale: architecture, unit economics, reliability, and the team that builds on all of it. This is high-scale technology marketplace infrastructure leadership, similar in shape and stakes to Twilio, Stripe, or Plaid. You’ll hire engineers excited to ship into something already used by millions, sharpen the platform as you run it, and build the first generation of agent-native infrastructure on top. Agents, not just humans, are becoming first-class callers of APIs, at machine speed and scale. The same primitives that made this marketplace work for developers (discovery, a single key, instant testing, programmable billing) are exactly what agents need, with an MCP foothold already on the platform. Agent-native discovery, agent-native commerce, and agent-native governance are not adjacent products to ship later. They are part of the thing we are building. Few platforms anywhere are as well-positioned to define how agents and APIs meet on the open internet, and few teams will get this chance. This is a leadership role with full technical authority. Ambitious, focused. Roles and Responsibilities Platform Architecture & Scale — Own end-to-end architecture across a multi-region AWS stack: management plane, runtime/proxy, commerce backbone, data plane, ~40 microservices. Design for horizontal scale, traffic spikes, and unpredictable backend APIs. Commerce Infrastructure — Own the usage ledger as a system of record. Keep metering, billing, invoicing, and publisher payouts on Stripe and PayPal accurate, auditable, and replayable. Developer, Consumer & Publisher Experience — Lift NPS through intuitive UI/UX, fast onboarding, clear diagnostics, and rapid time-to-first-successful-call. Reliability, Security & Abuse Prevention — Build resilience against free-tier abuse, key leakage, and malicious traffic. Own rate limiting, auth (OAuth2/JWT/mTLS), tenant isolation, and security posture. Vendor & Cost Discipline — Simplify a complex multi-vendor stack (monitoring, analytics, CDP, support, CDN). Drive consolidation, contract optimisation, and cloud cost reduction. Agent-Native Primitives — Build the first generation of agent-native primitives — discovery, commerce, and governance — into the platform. LLM-Enabled Engineering Productivity — Leverage advances in LLM-based coding and agentic tooling to evolve the software development process, improving engineering velocity, code quality, and cost efficiency across the stack. Engineering Organisation & Production Operations — Hire and lead the founding engineering organisation across platform, billing, data, UI/UX, and security; establish engineer-owned quality and on-call discipline. Leadership Partnership — Partner with the CEO, COO, and Financial Controller on strategy, vendor management, and unit economics. What success looks like The first generation of agent-native primitives — discovery, commerce, and governance — live in production, with growing agent traffic and architecture set up to compound. LLM-enabled coding and development workflows are deeply integrated into engineering, materially improving velocity, code quality, and cost efficiency. Reliability and security at marketplace scale — uptime ≥99.95%, billing and payouts publishers count on, security audits are clean. Developer and publisher experience that gets visibly better every quarter — activation, time-to-first-successful-call, dispute resolution, and trust metrics all climbing. A platform that gets cheaper to run as it grows, with a disciplined and consolidated software stack. An engineering org you’d want to join — full strength, owning production end-to-end, shipping at a confident cadence. What you bring to the role 10+ years of engineering leadership; built and grown teams from <10 to 100+ in platform or marketplace environments. Hands-on track record of scaling revenue-critical or commerce infrastructure without downtime; lived through scale-outages, billing disputes, or abuse/fraud incidents and fixed them. Hands-on AWS experience at scale (EKS, MSK / Kinesis, Aurora, Lambda, DMS) and ClickHouse / Snowflake / Kafka data stacks; fluency in at least one core platform language (Node.js/TypeScript, Go, Python, or Java). Some experience building or working with agentic systems and/or LLM-based applications. Distributed, event-driven systems running at scale in revenue-impacting environments; exposure to API gateways, rate limiting, quota enforcement, usage metering, or billing integration is a plus. Modern engineering practice across observability, SLOs, on-call, IaC, and safe rollouts. Security, compliance, and vendor discipline — zero-trust, secrets, SOC2/ISO27001, and consolidating engineering vendor stacks. Experience with API ecosystems; exposure to agent protocols (MCP, A2A, x402) is a plus. Bachelor’s or Master’s in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field; equivalent practical experience welcome. You build at the frontier. You build the team that builds with you. You build the cost discipline that lets innovation compound.

title: Product Designer (UX/UI, SaaS)
description: Mechanon · Full-time · On-site, Bangalore Compensation £7,800 – £13,200 per year. Anchored in GBP (Paid locally in INR equivalent), plus 0.25% equity in The Engine and a company performance bonus. About Us MECHANON is a Dubai-based venture studio that builds and incubates businesses from the ground up, with teams across Bangalore, Dubai and London. We're not an agency, consultancy or outsourcing company. We build and operate our own businesses, which means our team works directly on products from concept through to launch and growth. Our current focus is The Engine, a production intelligence platform for the film and television industry. The Role We're looking for our first Product Designer to take ownership of the product experience and design language of The Engine. This is a hands-on, high-ownership role for someone who is equally comfortable untangling a complicated product flow and obsessing over the final details of a UI. You'll work directly with the founder and our Platform Engineering Lead, taking product ideas and written specifications from early thinking through user flows, wireframes, prototypes and polished, developer-ready designs. You'll have significant influence over how the product works, not just how it looks. Because you're joining at the beginning, you won't inherit a large design organisation or an established system. You'll help create the foundations: the interaction patterns, visual language, components and design system that future parts of the product will be built on. A dedicated Front-End Engineer will work closely with you to turn those designs into the live product. What You'll Own Design the end-to-end user experience of The Engine across its core product Turn product requirements and rough ideas into clear flows, wireframes, prototypes and polished interfaces Establish and evolve our design system, including typography, colour, layout, components and interaction patterns Simplify complex, information-dense workflows into experiences that feel intuitive and fast Design search, discovery, filtering, dashboards and AI-assisted product experiences Design conversion-critical journeys including signup, trials, paywalls and upgrades Design responsive experiences across desktop, tablet and mobile Create developer-ready designs covering responsive behaviour, interactions, loading states, empty states and important edge cases Work directly with engineering throughout implementation to make sure the shipped product matches the design Help shape product decisions rather than simply receiving design tasks Who We're Looking For We're more interested in the quality, depth and judgement demonstrated in your shipped work than a specific number of years on your CV. You'll likely be a strong fit if you: Have designed and shipped real digital products, ideally SaaS platforms or complex web applications Are excellent at both UX and visual/UI design and don't see them as separate jobs Can take an ambiguous product problem from initial requirements through to a clear, buildable solution Have strong product judgement and can explain the reasoning behind your decisions Know how to make complex or information-dense interfaces feel simple Are highly proficient in Figma and comfortable building reusable, component-based design systems Understand responsive design and accessibility principles Produce clean, organised, developer-ready design files Work well directly with engineers and enjoy seeing your designs become real products Are comfortable moving quickly, iterating and receiving direct feedback Care deeply about craft without allowing perfectionism to prevent shipping Most importantly, we're looking for someone we can give a difficult product problem to and trust to take ownership of solving it. Nice to Have You don't need to have all of these, but we'd be especially interested if you've worked on: Data-heavy products, dashboards, analytics or admin tools Search, discovery, filtering or recommendation experiences AI-powered products or AI-assisted workflows B2B or B2C SaaS products Signup, checkout, subscription, paywall or trial-to-paid journeys Product analytics, activation, conversion and retention Early-stage products where the design system was still being established React-based products or close collaboration with modern frontend teams Motion, interaction design or advanced prototyping How We Work We're a small team and deliberately work with very little bureaucracy. You'll work closely with the people making product and engineering decisions, iterate quickly and see your work shipped rather than disappearing into long review processes. That environment suits designers who enjoy autonomy, direct communication and responsibility. This probably isn't the right role if you're looking for a large design organisation, highly structured design-review processes, purely conceptual work, or a remote/hybrid position. This is a fully on-site role in Bangalore, so you'll need to be based in Bangalore or willing to relocate. Why Join This is an opportunity to join at the point where the fundamental product experience is still being created. You'll have the chance to: Be the first designer and have genuine ownership over the product's design direction Establish the design language and systems rather than inherit them Work on a sophisticated product combining data, search, discovery and AI Work directly with the founder and engineering leadership See your work move quickly from Figma into production Participate in the upside of the product through 0.25% equity in The Engine How to Apply Apply through the Wellfound platform with your CV and portfolio. We're particularly interested in seeing real products you've shipped. Where possible, show us the problem you were solving, the decisions you made, what you personally owned and what ultimately made it into the product. Polished visuals are important, but we're just as interested in how you think. We look forward to finding out more about you. MECHANON

title: Senior Context Engineer
description: Company name: Springwood Digital Labs Private Limited Website: www.trypropel.ai Linkedin: Propel Job Title: Senior Context Engineer Location: HSR, Bangalore About Us: Propel is the first of its kind AI-native lifecycle marketing consulting firm specializing in delivering the entire value chain of campaign. We own the -technology -strategy -creativity -analytics -and the execution of campaigns Offering our clients a one-stop solution to meet their growing marketing needs. We have 4+ years of experience, serving 100+ clients with 80% of our clientele being early stage innovative startups from the US. As we target a $10M ARR milestone this year, we invite you to join our core team and help shape the future of marketing and consulting. About the Role Sonic is Propel's AI-native marketing platform. It pairs a chat-based agent with each marketer's brand, content, and the data sitting inside their existing marketing stack — campaign tools, product analytics, knowledge bases, communication channels — so they can move from a campaign brief to a live, executed campaign with fewer iterations and higher-quality output. Context is the moat. Everything Sonic produces is only as good as the context it pulls — each client's brand, their creative archives, the live data inside their marketing stack, and increasingly, what Sonic has learned from its own work. As Senior Context Engineer at Propel, you will own that surface end-to-end. The pipelines that bring brand assets, design language, copy archives, images, and live data from each client's marketing stack into Sonic. The storage and retrieval that make all of it activatable in milliseconds. The evaluation framework that proves the whole system is doing its job. You build it, you ship it, you monitor it. Your scope ends at a clean API. How that context is used inside the agent's prompts is owned by engineers downstream — you produce a high-quality, low-latency context surface; they decide how to weave it into the agent's reasoning. We are hiring for a trajectory. You join as Senior Context Engineer and grow into Staff Context Engineer scope within roughly six months — leading the architecture across all of context, with junior engineers contributing under your direction. What You Will Do Build and own the system that captures everything Sonic knows about each client's brand — brand guidelines, design language, copy archives, past creative, and other textual assets — and makes it queryable in milliseconds. Build and own the system that pulls live data from each client's existing marketing stack — campaign tools (e.g., Braze, Customer.io), product analytics (e.g., Mixpanel, Amplitude), knowledge bases (e.g., Notion), communication channels (e.g., Slack), and behavioral data (e.g., Fathom) — and normalizes it into context the agent can reason about. OAuth, rate limits, schema drift, and new integrations as the product grows. Build and own the system that brings non-textual context into Sonic — images today, with video and other modalities to follow — through embedding and retrieval choices appropriate to each modality. Build the loop that lets Sonic learn from itself — capturing what the agent did, what worked, what didn't, and the patterns across tool calls and user interactions, then feeding those learnings back as context that improves future runs. Design the end-to-end context pipeline — ingestion, chunking, vectorization, storage, retrieval, and delivery — with predictable latency, cost, and quality. Build the evaluation framework that measures whether context is actually doing its job — retrieval-quality metrics, agent-quality regression tests, and dashboards the team uses to catch problems before users do. You ship this yourself; you do not delegate it. Set the architectural direction for context across the platform — patterns the team builds on, decisions documented in writing, and junior engineers contributing under your direction. Author RFCs (Request for Comments) end-to-end — written design documents that specify the problem, alternatives considered, trade-offs, the decision, and what is explicitly not being built. Sharp enough that another engineer or an AI agent could build the right thing without you in the room. Mentor a junior engineer or intern - to ship-readiness on a scoped piece of the context surface. Ship through AI agents - Write specifications Claude (or equivalent) can execute against, review the output critically, and ship the result. Propel engineers do not measure their value in lines of code typed. Collaborate closely with the engineers who consume your context API, shaping what you produce to fit how the agent actually uses it. Required Competencies 5–7 years of total engineering experience, with at least 2–3 years on production context pipelines, retrieval-augmented systems, or retrieval at scale. Has shipped a production retrieval or context system and run the evaluations that prove it works. Both halves are required — we will ask for the specific evaluation design and what it caught. Hands-on builder. You can sit down and ship the evaluation framework yourself this week, not delegate it. Strong systems thinker. Opinions on vectorization choices, chunking strategy, retrieval ranking, hybrid search, and cost / latency trade-offs — and the ability to defend them. Has built or owned at least two integration connectors end-to-end (OAuth, rate limits, normalization). Comfortable in our stack: TypeScript, Node.js, PostgreSQL, vector storage (pgvector or equivalent). Strong adjacent stacks accepted if the ramp story is credible. Written communication strong enough to author RFCs that another engineer or an AI agent can build from without you in the room. AI-augmented engineering as a first-class part of your loop. If working through Claude (or equivalent) feels uncomfortable to you, this role is not a fit. Smart and curious — first-principles reasoning, comfortable in ambiguity, learns the next thing fast. Bonus: experience with multimodal context (image or video embeddings, multimodal retrieval); has worked on agent / tool-calling systems and understands the evaluation question for tool calls; experience with multi-tenant context isolation; has worked with Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers; has mentored a junior engineer to ship-readiness. How we measure performance Performance at Propel is measured on a written, six-axis rubric. Every engineer is evaluated on the same axes — what changes between levels is the bar, not the rubric itself. The six axes: Problem framing & specification — Can you describe what we should build, what we should explicitly not build, and why? Engineering judgement & verification — Do you instrument before you ship? Do you catch regressions before users do? System & architectural thinking — Can you reason about the system as a whole, not just the feature you're building? Product thinking & user affinity — Do you understand why the marketer cares about what you ship? Ownership & delivery — When you say you own something, do you mean it end-to-end? Collaboration & communication — Can your written work survive contact with a fresh engineer, an AI agent, or a designer who joined this week? Each axis is scored on a 1–5 scale. Review cadence: A written six-month checkpoint — lightweight re-score, no CTC change, feedback on which axes need to move and how. A full re-score at twelve months — promotion considered. Performance bonus: Up to 20% of fixed CTC, paid annually after the 12-month review, conditional on a small set of named outcomes agreed at the start of the role. If the bar is hit, the bonus pays. If it is not, the bonus does not pay. There are no surprises in either direction. Promotion to Staff Context Engineer: Considered at twelve months (and possible at the six-month checkpoint for exceptional trajectory). Promotion requires a rubric average of ≥ 4.5 with no individual axis below 4. What You Get Total target compensation between ₹35–45 LPA — fixed base plus performance bonus, anchored to our AI-native compensation framework. A written career path: Senior Context Engineer → Staff Context Engineer, with compensation recalibrated at promotion. Meaningful equity at founding-team scale, discussed at offer stage. A small, intentionally lean team where AI-augmented engineering is the operating model, not a buzzword.

hats Background in multi-tenant enterprise software: external integrations, enterprise workflows Strong testing culture: unit, integration, and e2e as a default, not an afterthought Containerization and CI/CD: Docker, Kubernetes, GitHub Actions Uses AI coding tools like Cursor or GitHub Copilot to move faster without compromising quality Experience with financial systems, billing platforms, or title: Principal Product Manager, Underwriting
description: About the role The Underwriting Engine is the most consequential system at Ethos. It determines who gets covered, at what price, and how fast — at scale, with accuracy that directly affects real families and carrier partners. Getting it right is as much a product problem as a technical one. We're looking for a Principal PM to own this platform through deep individual contribution. You'll set strategy and drive execution for the Underwriting Engine, including its rules infrastructure, knowledge graph, and workbench tooling, and work closely with Actuarial, Underwriting, Finance, and senior leadership across the US, Singapore, and India. There are no direct reports. This role is designed for someone who wants to go deep, not manage up. Your leverage comes from the quality of your thinking, the clarity of your communication, and your ability to move complex, high-stakes work forward entirely through influence. If you're energized by owning hard problems end-to-end without organizational scaffolding, this is the role. Duties and Responsibilities: Underwriting Engine: Rules Engine Own the decisioning rules infrastructure: how eligibility, pricing, and risk criteria are expressed, maintained, and updated at speed. Knowledge Graph Drive product strategy for how risk knowledge is structured, enriched, and made available to decisioning systems. Workbench Own the internal tooling that allows Actuarial and Underwriting teams to configure, test, and deploy decisioning changes safely. Roadmap & Stakeholder Alignment: Long-term roadmap Collaborate with Actuarial, Underwriting, Finance, and senior leadership to build and maintain a shared roadmap that serves end customers, the business, carrier partners, and internal users. AI/ML innovation Champion and drive a compliant AI/ML roadmap for underwriting, identifying where models improve accuracy, speed, and coverage, and working with data science and engineering to ship it. Protect families. Deliver accurate decisions. — The underwriting engine determines who gets life insurance and at what terms. Accuracy, fairness, and speed are product outcomes, not just engineering metrics. You'll own that accountability directly, as an individual. Qualifications and Skills: Deep individual operator You don't manage people you manage complexity. You're happiest when you're the one writing the PRD, running the stakeholder review, and driving the decision. You get things done through influence, rigor, and trust, not org structure. Platform-to-business translation You can walk into a conversation with a senior actuary and understand their constraints, then turn around and write a crisp product brief for engineering. You make complex technical systems legible to business stakeholders and vice versa, without losing fidelity in either direction. Data-informed decision making Comfortable in data-heavy environments where decisions have real downstream consequences. You know how to design experiments, read model outputs critically, and use data to prioritize ruthlessly without outsourcing judgment to dashboards. Structured communicator Your written and spoken communication is precise and concise. You can write a strategy doc that earns alignment across Actuarial, Engineering, and Finance without three rounds of revision — and present confidently to senior leadership across time zones without losing the room. Impact-driven prioritisation You have a strong filter for what matters. In a domain with near-infinite complexity, you consistently identify the highest-leverage investments and protect your own focus from everything else. You're comfortable saying no — and you say it with clear reasoning. Technical complexity without fear Rules engines, knowledge graphs, ML pipelines, decisioning systems — you've worked with systems of comparable complexity before. You don't need to be an engineer, but you need to be technically credible enough to make good build-vs-buy calls, spot architectural risks early, and earn respect from a strong engineering team. Proven track record in adjacent regulated domains Insurance experience is welcome but not required. We're looking for candidates who have built data-heavy decisioning or intelligence platforms at the intersection of compliance and regulation in credit, fraud, healthcare, risk, or similar fast-paced environments. What matters is the pattern: complex domain, high-stakes decisions, structured data at scale. #LI-Hybrid #LI-NG1

You'll drive the strategy and roadmap for the Underwriting Engine, including its rules infrastructure, knowledge graph, and the workbench tooling used by internal teams, and collaborate with Actuarial, Underwriting, Finance, and senior leadership across the US, Singapore, and India to build a long-term product vision that serves customers, the business, and our carrier partners equally. This is a high-trust, high-autonomy role. You'll lead a small team of 2–3 PMs and be expected to operate as a strong individual contributor yourself, connecting a complex technical platform to clear business outcomes, and championing AI/ML innovation in a domain where the stakes are high and the data is rich. Duties and Responsibilities: Underwriting Engine: Rules Engine: Own the decisioning rules infrastructure: how eligibility, pricing, and risk criteria are expressed, maintained, and updated at speed. Knowledge Graph: Drive the product strategy for how risk knowledge is structured, enriched, and made available to decisioning systems. Workbench: Own the internal tooling that allows Actuarial and Underwriting teams to configure, test, and deploy decisioning changes safely. Roadmap & Stakeholder Alignment: Long-term roadmap: Collaborate with Actuarial, Underwriting, Finance, and senior leadership to build a shared, durable product roadmap that serves end customers, the business, carrier partners, and internal users. AI/ML innovation: Champion and drive the AI/ML roadmap for underwriting — identifying where models can improve accuracy, speed, and coverage, and working with data science and engineering to ship it. Protect families. Deliver accurate decisions: The underwriting engine determines who gets life insurance and at what terms. Accuracy, fairness, and speed are product outcomes here — not just engineering metrics. You'll own that accountability directly. Qualifications and Skills: Operator who leads: You manage a small team but remain deeply involved in the work yourself. You set direction, unblock your PMs, and hold the bar on quality, without hiding behind process or headcount. When something is stuck, you fix it. Platform-to-business translation: You can walk into a conversation with a senior actuary and understand their constraints, then turn around and write a crisp product brief for engineering. You make complex technical systems legible to business stakeholders and vice versa, without losing fidelity in either direction. Data-informed decision making: You're comfortable in data-heavy environments where decisions have real downstream consequences. You know how to design experiments, read model outputs critically, and use data to prioritize ruthlessly without outsourcing judgment to dashboards. Structured communicator: Your written and spoken communication is precise and concise. You can write a strategy doc that earns alignment across Actuarial, Engineering, and Finance without three rounds of revision and present confidently to senior leadership in the US or Singapore without losing the room. Impact-driven prioritization: You have a strong filter for what matters. In a domain with near-infinite complexity, you consistently identify the highest-leverage investments and protect your team from everything else. You're comfortable saying no, and you do so with clear reasoning. Technical complexity without fear: Rules engines, knowledge graphs, ML pipelines, decisioning systems, you've worked with systems of comparable complexity before. You don't need to be an engineer, but you need to be technically credible enough to make good build-vs-buy decisions, spot architectural risks early, and earn respect from a strong engineering team. Proven track record in adjacent regulated domains: Insurance experience is welcome but not required. We're looking for candidates who have built data-heavy decisioning or intelligence platforms at the intersection of compliance and regulation in credit, fraud, healthcare, risk, or similar fast-paced environments. What matters is the pattern: complex domain, high-stakes decisions, structured data at scale. #LI-Hybrid #LI-NG1

title: Principal Security Engineer

Develop and enforce application security best practices across SDLC; partner with DevOps and engineering teams to integrate security into CI/CD pipelines. Evaluate and implement security tools, controls, and frameworks Provide technical leadership and mentorship to security engineers, software developers, and DevOps personnel. Lead response to complex security incidents or architectural flaws; conduct root cause analysis and recommend strategic remediations. Stay current with emerging threats, vulnerabilities, and security technologies, advising stakeholders on evolving risks and mitigations. AI Security Own the AI security program, including risk frameworks, threat models, and governance policies for AI/ML systems and LLM integrations. Review new AI tool features and model updates for security risks prior to adoption, covering prompt injection, data leakage, model poisoning, and supply chain threats. Track and apply industry guidance from NIST AI RMF, OWASP LLM Top 10, MITRE ATLAS, and CISA; translate standards into actionable internal controls and secure configuration baselines. Embed AI security reviews into the feature development lifecycle, including pre-deployment red-teaming and adversarial testing of AI-powered features. Monitor AI regulatory developments and advise on security and compliance implications for the organisation. Requirements Required Qualifications 10+ years of experience in security engineering or architecture roles. Bachelor’s degree in Cybersecurity, Information Technology, Computer Science, or related field from a reputable institution. Deep expertise in cloud platforms (particularly AWS), including infrastructure-as-code (e.g., Terraform, CloudFormation). Strong experience in secure software development and application security (e.g., OWASP Top 10, SAST, DAST, threat modeling). Experience designing and implementing zero-trust architectures, secure API gateways, and identity/access controls. Proficient in scripting or development languages (e.g., Python, Go, JavaScript) and secure coding practices. Demonstrated leadership in cross-functional security initiatives and technical mentorship. Hands-on experience assessing security risks of AI/ML systems, including familiarity with OWASP LLM Top 10, MITRE ATLAS, or NIST AI RMF. Demonstrated ability to evaluate new AI tool features and vendor releases for security implications, and to produce clear risk assessments and secure configuration guidance. Experience researching and applying industry security guidance, translating standards and frameworks into organisational controls and policies. Preferred Qualifications Certifications such as CISSP, CCSP, AWS Security Specialty, GIAC (GCSA, GWEB, GDSA). Familiarity with Kubernetes security, service mesh, and cloud-native security tooling. Experience in regulated industries (e.g., fintech, healthcare, SaaS at scale). Experience with AI red-teaming, adversarial ML, or LLM security assessment tooling. Familiarity with secure configuration benchmarks for AI/ML platforms (e.g., AWS Bedrock). Knowledge of emerging AI regulatory frameworks (e.g., EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF) and their security and compliance implications. #LI-Hybrid #LI-SP1

title: Staff Software Engineer
description: Our Purpose At Fiddler, we understand the implications of AI and the impact that it has on human lives. Our company was born with the mission of building trust into AI. The rise of Generative AI and Agents has unlocked generalized intelligence but also widened the risk aperture and made it harder to ensure that AI applications are working well. Fiddler enables organizations to get ahead of these issues by helping deploy trustworthy, and transparent AI solutions. Fiddler partners with AI-first organizations to help build a long-term framework for responsible AI practices, which, in turn, builds trust with their user base. AI Engineers, Data Science, and business teams use Fiddler AI to monitor, evaluate, secure, analyze, and improve their AI solutions to drive better outcomes. Our platform enables engineering teams and business stakeholders alike to understand the "what", “why”, and "how" behind AI outcomes. Our Founders Fiddler AI is founded by Krishna Gade (engineering leader at Facebook, Pinterest, Twitter, and Microsoft) and Amit Paka (product leader at Microsoft, Samsung, Paypal and two-time founder). We are backed by Insight Partners, Lightspeed Venture Partners, and Lux Capital. Why Join Us Our team is motivated to help build trust into AI to enable society harness the power of AI. Joining us means you get to make an impact by ensuring that AI applications at production scale across industries have operational transparency and security. We are an early-stage startup and have a rapidly growing team of intelligent and empathetic doers, thinkers, creators, builders, and everyone in between. The AI and ML industry has a rapid pace of innovation and the learning opportunities here are monumental. This is your chance to be a trailblazer. Fiddler is recognized as a pioneer in the field of AI Observability and has received numerous accolades, including: 2022 a16z Data50 list, 2021 CB Insights AI 100 most promising startups, 2020 WEF Technology Pioneer, 2020 Forbes AI 50 most promising startups of 2020, and a 2019 Gartner Cool Vendor in Enterprise AI Governance and Ethical Response. By joining our brilliant (at least we think so) team, you will help pave the way in the AI Observability space. At Fiddler, the Integrations Team owns the connective tissue between our customers' AI stacks and our observability platform. We build the OpenTelemetry-native SDKs, framework instrumentation, and ingestion pipelines that capture trace, metric, and model data from any environment — predictive models, LLMs, GenAI, and agentic applications — and land it reliably in Fiddler. This is a uniquely broad role. You'll operate simultaneously as an SDK/instrumentation lead, an OpenTelemetry expert, a distributed-systems architect, and an AI observability platform builder — owning everything from the decorator a developer adds to their agent, through OTLP ingestion, to the normalized telemetry that powers our product. If you're excited about OpenTelemetry, developer-facing SDKs, and meeting customers where their AI actually runs, this is the team. 🚀 What You'll Do Own the integration surface end-to-end: Design and build the SDKs, instrumentation libraries, and connectors — Fiddler OTel SDK, LangChain/LangGraph/Strands auto-instrumentation, LiteLLM, OTLP ingestion, and ML-platform connectors (Databricks, MLflow) — that bring customer telemetry and model data into a world-class AI observability platform. Make OpenTelemetry core, not adjacent: Own Fiddler's OTel and OTLP strategy — instrumentation libraries, collectors, exporters, sampling, and the end-to-end tracing path. Engage with the OpenTelemetry/OpenInference ecosystem and contribute back where it strengthens our integrations. Define agentic semantic conventions and mapping: Build the canonical abstraction layer that maps heterogeneous, non-deterministic agent frameworks (LangChain, LangGraph, Strands, custom Python agents, any OTLP source) onto Fiddler's unified span and metric model — framework-agnostic instrumentation that "just works." Lead distributed ingestion and processing systems: Architect the services and microservices that receive, normalize, persist, and expose ML + agentic observability signals (e.g., response relevancy, hallucination scores, multi-agent and tool-call traces) from raw trace data at enterprise scale, with strong guarantees around data integrity, ordering, and backpressure. Build for enterprise scale and trust: Design scalable data infrastructure, services, and APIs that handle high-throughput ingestion, meet compliance needs, and uphold SLAs. Champion developer experience: Treat our SDKs as products. Drive ergonomics (zero-boilerplate decorators, one-line setup), backward compatibility, versioning, docs, and reference examples so integrations take minutes, not weeks. Spearhead new evaluation and metric capabilities: Partner with product and customers on discovery, then build the new metrics and evaluation capabilities that evolving GenAI and agentic use cases demand. Raise operational maturity: Define and evolve reliability, latency, SLOs, and observability for the ingestion path. Champion improvements to CI/CD, testing frameworks, error handling, efficiency, and resiliency. Build the team & culture: Take an active role in growing a world-class engineering team — interviewing, evaluating candidates, mentoring, and coaching. 🎯 What We're Looking For Education & experience: Master's or Bachelor's in Computer Science or a related field, plus 10+ years of industry experience with a demonstrated, solid foundation in software development. OpenTelemetry depth: Hands-on experience with OpenTelemetry / OTLP — instrumentation, collectors, semantic conventions, sampling, and the broader tracing ecosystem. You understand telemetry generation and the systems that consume it. Backend & ingestion depth: Deep proficiency with Python and strong command of the technologies that power high-throughput ingestion — Kafka, Postgres, Redis — including the ability to design, build, and debug complex, large-scale streaming and storage systems. Integration & SDK mindset: Proven experience building developer-facing SDKs, client libraries, plugins, or data connectors, with strong instincts for API and contract design across systems you don't fully control. Adaptability & ownership: Proven ability to thrive in ambiguity and a fast-paced environment. A self-motivated initiator who takes ownership with high autonomy and confidently fills gaps when the full picture isn't available. System design & optimization: Strong grasp of distributed systems and the ability to troubleshoot production issues. Nice to have: cloud infrastructure (AWS/GCP, Kubernetes) and specialized databases (ClickHouse/Druid). Technical leadership & collaboration: Demonstrated ability to plan, execute, and deliver by breaking complex problems into manageable tasks and guiding a small team. Adept at cross-functional collaboration across a geographically distributed team — partnering with product managers, designers, frontend developers, and data scientists, and at times directly with customers and integration partners. Coaching & mentorship: An excellent collaborator and mentor who raises the technical bar for the whole team and regularly engages in code and design reviews. Good to Have Experience deploying and working with ML/LLM models in production, and comfort with modern LLM and agentic frameworks (e.g., LangChain, LangGraph, Strands, HuggingFace, vLLM, LiteLLM) and evaluation frameworks (e.g., Ragas, MLflow). Familiarity with ML platform ecosystems (Databricks, MLflow, SageMaker, Vertex AI) and the integration patterns that connect them to observability tooling. Contributions to open-source observability or instrumentation projects (OpenTelemetry, OpenInference, or similar). The posted range represents the expected salary range for this job requisition and does not include any other potential components of the compensation package and perks previously outlined. Ultimately, in determining pay, we'll consider your experience, leveling, location, and other job-related factors. Fiddler is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. If you require special accommodations in order to complete the interviews or perform job duties, please inform the recruiter at the beginning of the process. Beware of job scam fraud. Our recruiters use @fiddler.ai email addresses exclusively. In the US, we do not conduct interviews via text or instant message, or ask for sensitive personal information such as bank account or social security numbers.

title: Forward Deployed Engineer

You communicate effectively with both technical and business stakeholders, are comfortable leading architecture discussions and technical workshops, and thrive in environments where requirements evolve rapidly. You should be equally comfortable writing production-grade code, designing enterprise integrations and collaborating with customer teams. If you're excited about building enterprise-grade AI systems that create meaningful business impact, we'd love to hear from you.

title: Founding Engineer, RecruitmentTech
description: AI-native product · Global hiring market · Stealth / Pre-seed Remote-first · India preferred for time-zone overlap · Full-time We're a small founding team building something new in the global hiring market — an AI-native solution aimed at SMB and mid-market customers, currently in stealth. The hiring industry today is stuck in an AI doom loop. Job seekers use AI to apply; companies use AI to filter. Applications have surged past 11,000 per minute on LinkedIn alone, and only 8% of candidates believe the systems screening them are fair. Most of the tools sold to fix this are making it worse. We think the next generation of hiring software looks fundamentally different. We're building it. The founding team brings together a leader with years in global HR solutions and SaaS/enterprise hiring, a product leader who has scaled global systems in e-commerce and testing, and a GTM engineer who has taken a product from $1M to $20M ARR in 18 months. We've shipped at scale before. We're starting over — quietly, deliberately — on a problem we've each lived from a different side. About the role You'll be our first engineer. That phrase gets used loosely. We mean it literally — the first commit, the first architectural decision, the first deployment, the first hire after you. Every system that gets built later sits on top of what you build now. This is a founding seat with founding equity. You'll work alongside the three of us on product, technical, and hiring decisions, and shape how engineering culture takes root in this company. What you'll do Architect and build the core platform from line one — agents, retrieval, multi-tenant backend, data infrastructure, ranking and recommendation layers. Set the technical bar, the engineering culture, and the stack. Work directly with founders on product direction, customer conversations, and roadmap. Ship fast, iterate faster, in close loops with early design partners. Hire engineers two through five over the next 18 months, alongside the founding team. What we're looking for 5+ years of engineering experience, with real production work on AI systems — agents, RAG, recommendation engines, or similar. Prototypes don't count. Shipped systems do. Strong backend fundamentals — Python, distributed systems, multi-tenant architecture. Comfort across the stack: data pipelines, vector or graph stores, LLM orchestration, frontend when needed. title: Principal Engineer
description: *Role Overview * We are seeking a Principal Engineer who sets technical direction by example. An architect who still writes code, reviews code, and makes the engineers around them better. This is not a role for someone who has moved away from the keyboard. It is a role for an engineer who has shipped production systems at scale, knows the million small details that separate a demo from a product customers depend on. You will set architectural direction across our products and platforms. You will partner with our existing engineers, challenge their thinking, and ensure the systems we build are the best-architected they can be — simple, modular, resilient, and built to evolve. You will spend real time in code reviews, in design documents, and at the keyboard yourself. And you will invest heavily in the engineers around you: the strength of the team you grow is the truest measure of your success in this role. You understand that AI has fundamentally changed the job of a Principal Engineer — for the better. The best practitioners today ship more, review more, prototype more, and mentor more because they treat AI as an amplifier, not a threat. You will bring that mindset to DeepRunner, and you will help the rest of the engineering organization get better at it. *What You’ll Do * Set architectural direction across our products and platforms. Drive the decisions that matter: service boundaries, data models, API contracts, and the shape of the systems we will still be living with in three years. Write code. Ship code. Review code. Your tenure here will be measured in commits and architecture decisions, not slide decks. Raise the bar on code reviews. Every review is a teaching moment. Define the standards, enforce them, and explain the “why” so they stick. Mentor and grow the engineers around you. Develop your peers and your juniors into stronger engineers. This is a core responsibility of the role, not a side activity. Ship production software with full production responsibility: edge cases, failure modes, backwards compatibility, migrations, observability hooks. Always insist on the highest standards spanning architecture, development, deployment, operational excellence. Use AI in your daily work the way a modern Principal Engineer should: to prototype faster, review more code, explore more alternatives, and multiply your own reach. Qualifications Required 10+ years of hands-on software engineering with a clear track record of shipping production enterprise systems that customers depend on. Exemplary practitioner: still writes production-quality code, still does code reviews, and takes pride in it. Strong architectural judgment. Can design systems that are simple, modular, and resilient. Can spot over-engineering and under-engineering with equal confidence. Can explain trade-offs in plain language. Proven history of mentoring and developing other engineers — not just shipping personal work. Concrete examples of engineers whose growth you meaningfully accelerated. Deep grasp of the “million details” of shipping production software: edge cases, failure modes, backwards compatibility, migrations, zero-downtime changes. Active engagement with open source. Meaningful contributions to OSS projects, not just consumption. OSS is how great engineers learn from and teach each other, and we want that culture in-house. Fluent with modern AI coding assistants (Claude Code, Cursor, or similar). You understand that AI has changed the job of a Principal Engineer for the better, and you can articulate exactly how. Excellent written and spoken communication. Clarity is a core engineering skill at DeepRunner, not a soft skill. Preferred Startup experience. You have worked where you had to build, ship, and operate with a small team and a short runway. Track record of introducing architectural patterns or engineering practices that outlasted your tenure at the organizations where you worked. Comfortable working closely with distributed teams across geographies and time zones. Experience with AI/ML systems in production: LLM integrations, RAG pipelines, or agent architectures. *About DeepRunner AI * DeepRunner AI is building the future of SMB software. Our flagship product combines modern business platforms with AI-powered automation to help SMBs operate more efficiently. We believe AI should empower human workers by handling repetitive tasks so people can focus on strategic thinking, creativity, and complex problem-solving. We are a fast-growing startup with teams across Silicon Valley, Athens, and Delhi. Our culture is rooted in #Day1 and #OneTeam principles. We offer: Competitive salary, equity options, and benefits Opportunities for professional growth and development A dynamic and supportive work environment To learn more about DeepRunner AI and our vision, visit https://www.deeprunner.ai

title: Senior Frontend Engineer
description: Lyearn is an AI-native workforce intelligence platform. We help large organisations understand what their people are actually doing, what they're good at, and what's getting in their way — and then act on it. We're an unusual company. Ten years old, bootstrapped, and profitable — but the product you'd be joining is barely two years old, because we took the original platform apart and rebuilt it from the ground up. New architecture, new team, new thesis about what this category should be. That rebuild is roughly two-thirds done, and the next stretch is the part where the product has to look as intelligent as it is. Our customers are enterprises - a major private-sector bank, a high-growth commerce business, a global consumer brand - and they're demanding in exactly the way that makes work interesting. They notice everything. The role We're hiring one senior frontend engineer to own the visual and interaction layer of the product. Not a team lead, not a manager - an engineer whose work sets the standard for everything we ship. You would be the most senior frontend person in the company. That means real ownership: you make the calls on how our interfaces are structured, how our component layer evolves, and what "good" means here. It also means the work is visible. There's no layer of process between what you build and what a customer's VP sees on Monday morning. What you'll build Information-dense product surfaces. A sales leader opens Lyearn and sees two thousand opportunities distilled into the five things worth their attention today. A manager sees a skill footprint rendered as a radial chart that has to be legible at a glance and precise on inspection. An analytics module where the same underlying data reads completely differently depending on whether a CEO, a revenue leader, or an individual rep is looking at it. The hard part isn't any single screen. It's that every screen is an argument about what deserves attention - and it has to stay fast and readable while making that argument. Dense tables, custom visualisations, layered filtering, live data. This is closer to building a cockpit than building a website. Alongside the surfaces themselves, you'd own the component layer they're built from: the primitives, the patterns, the design tokens, and the consistency that makes a product feel like one product. Our stack React 19 · TypeScript · Vite · Tailwind v4 · GraphQL (urql) · recharts / d3 · Oxlint We're on modern versions deliberately and we keep them current. If you enjoy working on a codebase that isn't fighting five years of accumulated compromise, you'll like it here. What we're looking for You've shipped product UI at a genuinely high visual bar. You can take a Figma frame and land it exactly - spacing, weight, rhythm - and you're also the person who tells the designer when the frame is wrong, with a reason. You've done data-dense rendering for real. Virtualised lists, large tables, custom charts, interaction that stays smooth under load. You've hit a performance wall, measured it properly, and fixed it - and you can talk about that with specifics rather than adjectives. You think about GraphQL as a client architecture problem, not just a way to fetch things. Cache behaviour, fragment design, knowing when the shape of the data is the actual source of the bug. You build things other engineers build on. A component library, a design system, a set of primitives with a point of view - not just assembling someone else's. And you work well without a fully-specified ticket. We'll give you context, constraints, and a goal. What we need back is something real to react to, quickly. Roughly six or more years of frontend experience usually gets someone to this point, but we care much more about what you've shipped recently than about the number. How we work We ship weekly. We'd rather look at a rough version of the real thing on Tuesday than a polished plan for it in three weeks - most of our arguments get settled by building the thing and looking at it. Strong opinions are genuinely welcome. We're a small enough team that one person can change how the whole product feels, and we'd rather hear "this is wrong and here's why" early than discover it after launch. What we ask in return is that opinions move when the evidence does. You'd work closely with our Head of Engineering, our product designers, and the CTO. Decisions get made in hours, not sprints. Honest about what this isn't This isn't a large team with process cover. There will be weeks where priorities shift under you because an enterprise customer needed something. If you want scale and stability, there are better places. If you want your fingerprints on the whole thing, this is a good one. How to apply Apply here on Wellfound and send us a link to your work. Send us one thing you've built that's dense with information - a dashboard, a tool, an internal product, anything real. Along with it, two paragraphs about a rendering or data-layer problem inside it that you solved, ideally with the numbers. We read every one of these properly, and we'll get back to you either way.

title: Product Designer (UI / Visual Craft)
description: We make functional things beautiful. We need someone who's better at that than we are. Lyearn is an AI-native employee operating system. Legacy HR software is blind to how work actually happens - we make it visible. In practice that means a lot of real, dense product: dashboards, deal-intelligence views, performance signals, learning surfaces. Our standard isn't "usable." It's beautiful. You'd own the visual craft of that product. We hand you a workflow and the intent; you turn it into pixel-precise UI that an engineer can build without guessing. You report straight to the leadership, on a small team with no layers and no design-by-committee. You'll thrive here if: Your portfolio makes people stop scrolling - and it's full of interface work. Screens, dashboards, real apps. Not logos, posters, or brand decks. You can make information-dense UI beautiful. Tables, analytics, multi-state components — the hard stuff, not just hero sections and landing pages. You sweat the 4px and you have enough product sense to run without hand-holding. Nice, not required: Motion / micro-interaction chops. Design-system experience. Curiosity about shipping in code (React / Tailwind). You won't touch the stack day one, but we'll train you if you want to grow into design-engineering.

across the full stack — from application layer to database internals Integrate and troubleshoot platform features Internal Collaboration Support internal teams, including Solutions and Customer customer issues through cross-team knowledge sharing Innovation & Growth Use AI to accelerate your work Contribute to platform improvements based on real-world customer needs Stay current with complex issues that span multiple parts of the stack You contribute to making our platform more reliable and performant Your team relies on your versatility and problem-solving abilities You're continuously learning and sharing knowledge with the team What We're Looking For Must-Have Skills Strong PostgreSQL knowledge — You understand query optimisation, indexing strategies, execution plans, and database internals Proficiency in CLI — Comfortable in command-line SQL expertise — Complex queries, window functions, CTEs, and PL/pgSQL don't intimidate you Performance analysis — Reading logs, metrics, and identifying bottlenecks Experience with TimescaleDB, other relational databases Background in customer-facing technical roles Curiosity or experience with AI in databases Ability to learn architecture Kubernetes — Understanding of container orchestration, pods, services, and resource management Browser DevTools debugging — Using browser console, Network tab, and developer tools to title: Infrastructure Engineer (DevOps) — SDE2
description: About the role Pratilipi is building a generational company in storytelling, and infrastructure is core to that bet. We're looking for an Infrastructure Engineer — a hands-on role embedded in a high-growth product team using AWS, CI/CD, our self-managed data layer, and the operational substrate for the AI workloads now landing in production. You'll help us self-host our own models and take the infrastructure multi-region as we expand globally. Expect a lot of breadth, with depth in a few things that matter. You won't be a specialist hiding behind a narrow remit — you'll move across AWS, CI/CD, databases, CDN, and AI infra, and go deep where it counts. What you'll do Own our AWS infrastructure through Terraform — ECS on EC2, VPCs, IAM, autoscaling, rolling deploys. Clickops-free console as the target. Build Jenkins pipelines that are fast, safe, and self-serve. Be in the deploy paths, not just the platform. Drive cost optimisation. Own media delivery at scale — Cloudflare CDN, image/video/audio transcoding, format/device delivery — tuned for latency, cache hit ratio, and egress cost. Operate the self-managed data layer with service teams — RDS MySQL, MongoDB, Valkey, plus managed MSK and ScyllaDB Cloud. Lead migrations end-to-end (e.g. the ongoing Redis → Valkey). Stand up the operational substrate for AI in production — GPU capacity, inference gateways, key rotation, rate limits, cost-per-request visibility. Build observability for LLM agents: traces, token/cost accounting, eval hooks, alerts on silent regressions. Partner with the AI/ML team on self-hosting models — capacity planning, vLLM / TGI serving, canary rollouts, and cost/latency trade-offs vs managed providers. Own reliability across services and infra — SLOs, alerting, incident response, blameless postmortems. Move teams from firefighting to proactive reliability. Once you have the context, add the guardrails — IaC checks, deploy gates, paved paths — that make the right thing the easy thing and quietly remove whole classes of human error. What we're looking for 4–6 years in DevOps, SRE, or infrastructure — production systems at meaningful scale, with ownership beyond tickets. A problem solver with high agency. You reason from first principles, don't wait to be told, and dig in rather than deflect — whether it's a developer stuck on Terraform or an ML engineer asking for GPUs. Strong AWS hands-on — ECS on EC2, VPCs, IAM, multi-AZ design — and proficiency with Terraform (you write modules others reuse). Jenkins in production plus a real sense of developer experience in CI/CD — you've looked at deploy-time metrics and changed them. Python, Ansible, and shell — you automate work rather than repeat it. Operated databases in production — at least some of RDS MySQL, MongoDB, Redis/Valkey. Done migrations, failovers, and perf tuning, not just provisioning. Working familiarity with Kafka and Cassandra/ScyllaDB. Strong grasp of Linux internals and networking fundamentals (TCP/IP, DNS, TLS, load balancing) and common failure modes. Some hands-on exposure to LLM-based systems — inference endpoints, agent tracing, token/cost, or evals in CI. Not a researcher; you should reason clearly about latency, cost, and failure modes of LLM workloads. Comfortable with cloud security fundamentals: IAM least-privilege, secrets management, network segmentation. Prior exposure to ISO 27001 / DPDP-style controls is a plus. Tech stack AWS · ECS (on EC2) · Terraform · Jenkins · Ansible · Python · Cloudflare · Prometheus · Grafana · InfluxDB · RDS MySQL · MongoDB · Valkey · MSK · ScyllaDB Cloud · growing: GPU inference · vLLM / TGI · OpenTelemetry GenAI · Langfuse-style tracing · multi-region AWS Security & Data Handling All employees are expected to handle sensitive data responsibly in compliance with the DPDP Act, ISO-27001:2022, and Pratilipi's internal security policies — ensuring data privacy, confidentiality, and NDA obligations at all times.

title: Senior Full-Stack Engineer
description: The Role As the first full-time engineer at ADOSX, you will build the foundations that future teams inherit. You are the engineer who turns the architecture into the product people touch. You work across the whole stack, Django and DRF on the back and Next.js and React on the front, and you own the features end to end. Where the architect owns the dangerous core, you own the breadth: shipping the features and screens that make the product usable day to day, and building the integrations that feed them. You build agentically. AI coding agents are part of your daily toolkit and a big reason you ship fast. You'll spend time inside dealerships, work closely with customers, and build systems grounded in operational reality—not assumptions. What you'll own Features end-to-end : You take a feature from data model to API to UI without hand-offs: the Django models, the DRF endpoints, and the Next.js screens, each built cleanly within the architect's boundaries. The in-house integrations : Build and maintain the integrations to the external systems. These are built in-house rather than bought, so you own the protocol quirks, the version drift, and the reliability. The user-facing app : The Next.js and React front end: the dashboard shell, data tables, the AI chat surface, and the mobile-first screens for users who are often on a phone in the field. Messaging and scheduled flows : The customer-messaging integration (inbound webhooks, queued outbound) and the scheduled jobs behind reminders, follow-ups, and daily insight delivery. Quality on your surface area: Tests, sensible error handling, and never breaking tenant isolation or the audit trail, including when reviewing AI code. What we're looking for Solid full-stack delivery : Django and DRF plus React and Next.js, comfortable owning a feature from database to UI on your own. Agentic development as a habit: You use AI coding agents fluently to move faster, and you review their output as carefully as a teammate's. You have caught the subtle bugs they introduce. Integration grit : You have wired up a fiddly third-party system and made it reliable, and you do not flinch at messy upstream formats. PostgreSQL fluency : You write the tenant filter every time and understand why. Pragmatic and shippy : You prefer a working, tested feature today over a perfect one next month, and you can estimate honestly. A collaborator. You will pair with and unblock the juniors, and review their work. Nice to have * Celery or async experience, and front-end depth such as styled-components or a CSP-aware setup. * Prior work integrating accounting, messaging, or other enterprise platforms. * First six months, what good looks like * The core transactional flow of the product works end to end in the user-facing app. * The key in-house integrations are live and reliable on the pilot. * The user-facing screens reuse a consistent component language and hold up on a mid-range phone. You'll Thrive Here If * You love ambiguity more than certainty. * You prefer ownership over instructions. * You think in systems, not tickets. * You enjoy getting your hands dirty with customers. * You learn by building rather than waiting. * You use AI as leverage, not as a substitute for judgment. * You want both the 0→1 and 1→100 journeys.

title: Junior Full Stack Engineer
description: The Role You are early in your career and here to grow fast on a real, hard product. You take well-defined tasks across the stack, a slice of an API, a screen, a scheduled job, a set of tests, and deliver them well, with the architect and senior engineer guiding you. You are expected to build agentically from day one, using AI coding agents to learn faster and ship more while learning to judge what they get wrong. Over time you grow into owning whole features end to end. You'll spend time inside dealerships, work closely with customers, and build systems grounded in operational reality—not assumptions. What you'll own Build well-scoped pieces across the stack: Django models, serializers, and tasks on the back end, and React and Next.js screens and components on the front, within the patterns the architect sets. Work close to real data : Help build the integrations that bring in a dealer's data and the tooling that makes it inspectable, learning how messy real-world data becomes something trustworthy. Use AI agents well : Lean on AI coding assistants to move faster, but learn to read and verify what they produce rather than pasting it blindly, especially on anything touching money or another dealer's data. Write tests, including the unglamorous but vital ones that protect tenant isolation. You will learn early why these matter. Fix, instrument, and document. Chase down a bug, add logging, write the runbook entry. The connective tissue of a real system. What we're looking for Foundations across the stack : some Python and some JavaScript or React, from internships, projects, or self-teaching. We care how you think, not your years. Already building with AI tools : You use AI coding assistants on your own projects and are keen to get sharper at directing and checking them. Care about correctness : You double-check, you test, and you would rather ask than guess on something that matters. Fast learner, low ego : You take feedback well, read code to understand it, and are not afraid to say “I don't know that yet.” Basic SQL and a willingness to get genuinely good at it. Nice to have Any Django, React, Celery, or SQL exposure, curiosity about LLMs and agentic workflows, and comfort on the command line and with Git. You'll Thrive Here If * You love ambiguity more than certainty. * You prefer ownership over instructions. * You think in systems, not tickets. * You enjoy getting your hands dirty with customers. * You learn by building rather than waiting. * You use AI as leverage, not as a substitute for judgment. * You want both the 0→1 and 1→100 journeys. The Hard Truth Early-stage startups are hard. There will be ambiguity, changing priorities, and periods of intense execution because building from zero demands it. But you'll own products end-to-end, work directly with founders and customers, and likely learn more in two years than many engineers do in ten. If building the intelligence layer for Indian automotive retail excites you more than maintaining systems someone else designed, we'd love to build ADOSX together.

title: Principal Product Manager, AI Applications
description: You are a Principal Product Manager that will lead key deliverables within Augury’s agentic industrial workforce. This role sits at the intersection of industrial AI, process health, IoT, enterprise software, and operational workflows. You will define and scale agentic products that automate and optimize customer production capabilities and generate Augury’s new agentic SKUs. You will partner closely with Engineering, Data Science, Design, GTM, Operations, and strategic customers to take products from concept through launch and adoption. This is a highly strategic and hands-on role for someone who thrives in complex environments and enjoys turning ambitious ideas into scalable products with measurable customer impact. What You’ll Own Agent for Operational Processes You will own Augury’s Operations Agent — a persona-based AI agent built for production operations teams, process engineers, and shift supervisors. The Operations Agent connects to customer historians, process systems, and production data to monitor KPIs continuously, surface anomalies and root-cause hypotheses before they become incidents, and progress toward autonomous recommendations within customer-defined guardrails. You will drive this product from active design-partner validation through commercial launch. Agent for Exploration You will own the Industrial Data Exploration Agent — Augury’s cross-source investigation surface that enables reliability engineers, RSMs, and site users to query across machine health data, CMMS work orders, and historian process data through a unified natural language experience. Where today’s users navigate disconnected systems to build a single machine narrative, the Exploration Agent brings that context together in one conversation. This agent is both a standalone product and the shared intelligence surface that every persona-based agent in Augury’s suite builds on. Additional Agentic Applications You will define and sequence Augury’s emerging agent portfolio beyond the initial suite — including agents for maintenance planning, corporate intelligence, and cross-site analysis — and shape the longer-horizon vision for an Agent and Workflow Studio that enables customers to configure and deploy tailored industrial AI experiences across their operations. This means translating validated design-partner signals into prioritized expansion bets, developing the commercialization model for multi-agent offerings, and positioning Augury as the central platform for industrial data, intelligence, and action. What You Bring 10+ years of technical Product Management or equivalent product leadership experience Experience building and launching AI (agentic) applications Deep familiarity with industrial environments — manufacturing, operations, maintenance, reliability, or supply chain — and the personas who work in them Experience and understanding of building complex data systems Proven track record taking complex products from ambiguity through launch and commercial impact — without someone defining the problem for you first Familiarity with AI-native product development — you can drive decisions on agentic systems, LLM evaluation, and production AI reliability without needing an engineer to translate Strong cross-functional leadership skills across Engineering, Design, Data Science, GTM, and customer-facing teams Strong analytical, communication, and stakeholder management skills Comfortable operating in fast-moving, ambiguous environments Preferred Experience at both large and small operations Experience with industrial data sources: process historians, CMMS platforms, or equivalent operational enterprise systems Experience with conversational AI, natural language interfaces, or AI-assisted workflow products Experience partnering with design partners or strategic enterprise customers to co-develop and launch new product offerings Why This Role Matters Augury has spent over a decade building the world’s most trusted machine health platform — helping global manufacturers prevent failures, reduce unplanned downtime, and protect their most critical production assets. Now we are making a harder and more important bet: that AI agents can do more than alert and inform — they can reason, recommend, and act alongside the people running the world’s most critical production environments. The agents you build here will not be demos or experiments. They will be deployed in active plants, used by real operators, and measured by the value they create in production. You will not be managing a feature roadmap — you will be defining what industrial AI looks like in practice, for some of the world’s largest industrial organizations.

title: Remote Operations Engineer

This is a unique opportunity to move from traditional on-site process engineering to a tech-forward, remote role where you will directly influence the scalability of AI in manufacturing. A Day In Your Life Continuous Monitoring: Utilize AI-powered dashboards to monitor production performance, process conditions, and critical operating metrics for industrial manufacturing lines. Anomaly Management: Review AI-generated alarms and process deviations; surface and prioritize anomalies to ensure operational continuity. Real-time Coordination: Act as a critical liaison between Augury's AI insights and on-site personnel, guiding operational workflows and supporting operators with day-to-day decisions via Teams or VoIP. Documentation & Handoffs: Maintain meticulous operational logs and key event documentation, ensuring structured handoffs between night shifts and day-time on-site teams. Domain Expertise: Provide human-in-the-loop escalation support, applying your manufacturing background to troubleshoot complex industrial process issues. What You Bring Educational Background: Bachelor’s degree in Process Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Manufacturing Operations, or a related technical field. Industry Experience: 4–8 years of experience operating, monitoring, troubleshooting, and optimizing industrial manufacturing processes. Technical Proficiency: Hands-on experience with industrial systems including DCS, SCADA, Historians (e.g., AVEVA), and Industrial Automation. Analytical Mindset: Proven ability to analyze complex data sets and draw professional conclusions to improve manufacturing efficiency and yield. Communication: Excellent verbal and electronic communication skills, with the ability to lead technical discussions and build credibility with on-site engineering teams. Nice to Have Continuous Improvement: Experience with Six Sigma, Lean Manufacturing, or Process Optimization methodologies. Instrumentation & Controls: Familiarity with I&C systems and wireless OT connectivity protocols. AI/ML Interest: A passion for how AI agents can reduce routine monitoring loads and enhance human decision-making.

title: Machine Learning Engineer
description: Augury is building AgenticAI systems that transform how industrial organizations understand and optimize their operations. As a Senior ML Engineer on this team, you will help turn that vision into reality. You will be part of the AgenticAI team, you will work closely with central Algorithm and Product teams to design, build, and deploy intelligent systems that power next-generation industrial AI applications. You will own the end-to-end lifecycle of machine learning solutions—from problem definition and data exploration to model development, deployment, and production monitoring. Your work will span classical machine learning, time-series modeling, and generative AI to build agent-based systems that turn complex industrial data into actionable intelligence. You will architect and implement Agentic applications that leverage heterogeneous data sources, including sensor-based time-series signals, unstructured text, and existing ML frameworks. These systems will directly power customer-facing workflows, delivering measurable operational impact for industrial manufacturers. This role sits at the intersection of Agentic AI and Industrial AI, where your work will directly shape how customers interact with Augury’s platform and realize value from their data. A Day In Your Life Own the full machine learning lifecycle: problem scoping, data exploration, pipeline development, model training, deployment, and monitoring in production. Design and build Agentic AI systems that combine time-series modeling, signal processing, and generative AI (LLMs, embeddings, orchestration frameworks, and tool use). Develop and deploy machine learning models for forecasting, anomaly detection, and pattern recognition in industrial sensor data. Integrate classical statistical methods, deep learning, and GenAI techniques to generate actionable insights from complex datasets.
