title: Senior DevOps Engineer
description: Location: BLR, Onsite Company: Neoflo.ai (Headquartered in Singapore) About Neoflo Neoflo.ai is an early-stage startup rethinking how enterprise workflows should work in an AI-first world. Our mission is to fundamentally rewire how enterprises think about business processes, whether it is outbound sales, seller onboarding, or document-heavy workflows across finance, logistics, insurance, and healthcare. Think: billions of PDFs, emails, and faxes that still require armies of people to interpret and act on. We believe AI can—and should—do the heavy lifting. We’re building a universal AI context engine that interprets these documents, learns patterns, and either automates actions or drastically reduces human effort. Think: "GPT for back-office ops" meets "Zapier for messy business workflows" meets “Human judgment and accountability of BPOs.” About the Role We’re looking for a hands-on DevOps Engineer who has scaled production AI/ML systems and treats reliability as a product. You will own the infrastructure that runs Neoflo: the deployment pipelines, the GPU fleet, the observability layer, and everything between a model checkpoint and a paying customer. This is a founding-team role. You are not just keeping the lights on. You are designing the platform our engineers ship on, and the cost structure our gross margins depend on. In this role, you will: DevOps Engineer, Founding Team 2 • Own the infrastructure end-to-end across our cloud footprint (AWS / GCP), including VPC design, IAM, secrets management, and multi-region setups for SOC 2 and customer data residency requirements. • Build and maintain CI/CD pipelines that take code from commit to production in minutes, with automated tests, canary rollouts, and one-click rollback. • Operate our LLM and VLM serving stack. This includes GPU capacity planning, autoscaling inference workloads, optimizing cold-start latency, and managing spend across self-hosted models and third-party APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, etc.). • Stand up observability that actually catches problems before customers do: structured logs, traces, metrics, model-quality monitoring, and on-call alerting that doesn’t cry wolf. • Drive infrastructure cost down as a workstream. Track unit economics per workflow, identify the top spend drivers, and ship fixes. • Harden the platform for enterprise customers: SOC 2, audit logging, data isolation, encryption at rest and in transit, and the security reviews that come with selling to CFOs. You Might Be a Fit If You... • Have 5+ years of DevOps, SRE, or platform engineering experience, with at least 2 years running production workloads that include ML or LLM inference. • Are fluent with AWS, and have shipped infrastructure as code in Terraform or Pulumi. • Have hands-on experience with Kubernetes in production: networking, autoscaling, GPU node pools, and the failure modes that come with each. • Know your way around the Python ecosystem well enough to read service code, debug containers, and write tooling, even if you don’t ship features yourself. • Have built and owned CI/CD pipelines (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, ArgoCD, or similar) that real engineering teams depend on. • Can stand up an observability stack (Prometheus / Grafana / OpenTelemetry / Datadog) and know what to monitor, not just how to install it. • Operate with extreme ownership. When production breaks at 2 AM, you don’t wait to be paged twice. When cloud spend spikes, you find out why before the finance team asks. • Can break down vague, ambiguous infra requirements into concrete, shippable plans, and push back when the right answer is “we don’t need this yet.” Nice to Have • Experience serving open-source LLMs or VLMs in production (vLLM, TGI, Triton, Ray Serve), including quantization, batching, and GPU memory tuning. • Background taking a company through SOC 2 Type II or ISO 27001, end to end. • Experience with GPU cost optimization at scale: spot capacity, reserved instances, multi-cloud arbitrage, or self-hosted clusters. • Experience with data infrastructure (Postgres at scale, vector stores, queues like Kafka or SQS, workflow orchestrators like Temporal or Airflow). • Prior experience in a startup or early-stage environment where you’ve had to wear multiple hats and ship without a playbook.

title: Senior Test Engineer
description: Job Title: Senior Test Engineer (4+ Years Experience) Location: Bengaluru, On-Site Role Overview: We are looking for a Senior Test Engineer with deep expertise in functional API testing and test automation. This role sits at the intersection of Quality Assurance and Product Engineering, requiring close collaboration with developers, product managers, and cross-functional teams to ensure high-quality software delivery. The ideal candidate is technically strong, ownership-driven, and capable of independently designing and maintaining scalable automation frameworks while championing quality practices across the SDLC. Key Responsibilities: Design, build, and maintain robust API and UI test automation frameworks from scratch. Perform comprehensive API testing — functional, integration, contract, and load — across REST and GraphQL interfaces. Write and execute test plans, test cases, and exploratory charters for new features and regression cycles. Integrate automated tests into CI/CD pipelines for continuous quality feedback. Identify, log, and track defects using JIRA with clear reproduction steps, severity tagging, and root-cause documentation. Conduct performance and load testing using tools like k6, Locust, or JMeter to validate system behavior under stress. Drive test coverage analysis, gap identification, and quality metrics reporting to stakeholders. Collaborate with developers during code reviews to ensure testability and early defect prevention. Lead regression, smoke, and release validation efforts independently. Mentor junior QA engineers and promote quality best practices across the team. Mandatory (Non-Negotiable) Requirements: 4+ years of hands-on QA experience with a strong focus on API and automation testing. Deep understanding of REST API concepts — HTTP methods, status codes, authentication (OAuth2, JWT, API keys), request/response validation. Proficiency in at least one automation language: Python, JavaScript, or Java. Hands-on experience with UI and API automation frameworks such as Pytest-requests, RestAssured, or Playwright. Experience designing test automation architecture — not just writing tests, but structuring maintainable, scalable frameworks. Strong understanding of SDLC, defect lifecycle, and shift-left testing principles. Familiarity with CI/CD concepts and pipeline integration for automated test execution. Required Skills & Tools Postman / Apidog — advanced API testing, collections, environments, and scripting. Selenium / Pytest / Playwright — automation framework development and maintenance. JMeter / k6 / Locust — load and performance testing. JIRA — defect tracking, test cycle management. Git — version control, branching strategy, code review participation. CI/CD Tools — GitHub Actions, Jenkins, or equivalent for pipeline integration. SQL / NoSQL basics — database validation as part of end-to-end test coverage. Good to Have: Exposure to AI/ML systems testing or responsible AI evaluation frameworks. Knowledge of contract testing tools such as Pact. Experience with agentic testing architectures or MCP-based tooling. Background in VAPT revalidation or security-adjacent QA workflows. Familiarity with Agile/Scrum ceremonies and sprint-based delivery. About PrivaSapien: With Privacy regulations coming across the globe, all data centric business models using or abusing personal data are being disrupted. Moreover every business is becoming a data business today. Hence, Privacy engineering is the need of the hour globally to meet the emerging requirements and establishing digital trust with customers & regulators, across industry verticals. PrivaSapien is a pioneering and award-winning privacy deep tech research company working towards building a spectrum of Privacy Enhancing Technology based products and services to unlock data without violating people’s privacy. PrivaSapien has won Niti Aayog’s Aatmanirbhar Bharath Award, Data Security Council of India’s Privacy Challenge in two categories of ‘Purpose limitation’ and ‘Privacy due diligence’. We are currently working with Indian, American, European and Japanese companies across industry verticals like Healthcare, Automobile, Advertisement, Consulting, Insurance, Telcos etc and also some Indian govt PSUs to unlock data without violating people’s privacy. We have recently secured funding from a reputed US VC firm. We have also filed multiple international privacy engineering patents. Our Vision & Work Culture: Vision: PrivaSapien’s vision is to innovate and drive the “Evolution of the privacy era”. PrivaSapien strongly believes that privacy is a fundamental right in the digital era. Without privacy, human being’s thoughts, emotions, buying behavior and even voting can be manipulated with their own data and make humans AlgoSalves. Hence, PrivaSapien builds privacy engineering products, platforms and services that make digital experiences safer for humanity, at the same time creating strategic advantage for businesses in the privacy era. Passion: PrivaSapiens are a group of people who are extremely passionate about privacy and are crazy enough to believe that we can protect privacy of every person across the world, using our innovate products and services. Integrity & Trust: At PrivaSapien, Integrity is a fundamental uncompromisable tenet. Integrity creates trust and trust is the foundation for any long-term relationship & ultimately success, especially in the area of privacy, where customer trusts us with their data. Customer first, Customer last: We are obsessed with customer value creation. Every action and decision at all levels will be based on customer’s requirements and preference in mind. Adaptability: As Charles Darwin stated, “The species that survives is the one that is able best to adapt and adjust to the changing environment”. In these interesting and disruptive times, more than your skills, your adaptability to emerging requirements is the key to success. Innovation: We are an innovative Company at the core of everything we do. Each employee is empowered to be innovative in every aspect of their job and is expected to set the standard for the industry to follow. Perseverance: PrivaSapien strongly believes that there is no substitute to hard work. Privacy is the right thing to do, but it is an uncharted territory. At ‘PrivaSapien’, we persevere to create and show the world the right path to privacy. But it’s not easy, so be prepared for lots of learning’s, challenges and burning lot of midnight oil. title: Technical Co-Founder / Founding Product Engineer — Vertical SaaS | Equity Only
description: Building the operating system for modern tattoo studios. I'm building Limespun, a vertical SaaS platform designed specifically for tattoo studios, studio owners, and tattoo artists. Our goal is ambitious but simple: Give a tattoo studio one beautifully designed system to run almost its entire business. From bookings and client management to artists, multiple locations, daily operations, workflows, studio management, compliance, communication, reporting, and eventually much more. We're initially focused on the US, UK and other English-speaking markets, with the ambition to build a serious global vertical SaaS company. The product is already actively being built — this is not just an idea looking for someone to create an MVP. Now I'm looking for a technical co-founder who wants to build the company with me. Important: This Is a Co-Founder Role This is not a salaried engineering position. This is currently a 100% equity-based opportunity. There is no salary at this stage. I'm looking for someone who genuinely wants to own part of a company, take a long-term bet on what we're building, and create something valuable together. Meaningful co-founder equity will be offered based on: Experience Technical ability Level of commitment Responsibility Long-term involvement Overall founder fit Standard founder vesting would be part of the structure. If you're primarily looking for freelance work, consulting income, or an immediate salary, this won't be the right opportunity. What You'd Build With Me You would become the technical counterpart to me as founder. You'll have genuine influence over: Product architecture Backend and frontend engineering Database architecture APIs and integrations Infrastructure Security and scalability Engineering quality AI-assisted development Technical product decisions Developer tooling and automation Future engineering hiring Technical roadmap decisions The current stack includes technologies such as Next.js, TypeScript, Supabase/Postgres and modern cloud infrastructure. I'm already using AI heavily to accelerate product development. I don't need someone who is against AI-assisted development. I want someone who understands how to use AI as an engineering multiplier while still having the technical depth to know when the AI is wrong. Someone who can architect, review, debug, simplify and make good engineering decisions rather than blindly accepting generated code. You Won't Only Be Coding This part is important. Limespun is a vertical SaaS product. To build an exceptional vertical SaaS company, we need to understand tattoo studio owners extremely deeply. I want my technical co-founder to occasionally be comfortable speaking directly with customers. That could include: Customer discovery calls Product feedback sessions Product demos Understanding workflow problems Discussing technical/product questions Helping during onboarding when necessary Seeing first-hand how customers actually use what we've built You do not need to be a salesperson. But I don't want a technical founder who hides behind tickets and never wants to speak with users. I want us both to understand our customers. What I'll Own I don't expect you to do everything. I'll primarily take responsibility for: Company operations Product vision Product strategy Roadmap Prioritization Customer feedback management Critical product thinking UX/product direction Business decisions Team coordination Go-to-market development Partnerships and growth as we scale We'll make important company and product decisions together. I want this to feel like two founders building one company, not a founder giving tasks to a developer. The Person I'm Looking For Technical skill matters. But founder compatibility matters just as much. I'm looking for someone who is: Highly curious You naturally explore problems instead of waiting for instructions. Product-minded You think about users and outcomes, not only code. Low ego You're comfortable challenging ideas and equally comfortable changing your mind when someone else has a better answer. Mature Startups have problems. I want someone who discusses them calmly instead of creating unnecessary drama. Open-minded We're going to experiment, learn, fail occasionally and change things quickly. Friendly and easy to work with We're potentially going to spend years building together. I genuinely care that we enjoy working with each other. Independent You can turn an unclear product problem into a technical solution without needing a detailed specification for everything. Reliable If we agree to something, I should be able to trust that it'll happen — and the same should be true for you with me. Customer-friendly You're comfortable communicating clearly with non-technical people. Excited about ownership You want to say, "We're building this," rather than "I'm working for this startup." Technical Background I'd Love You don't need to match every item. Strong experience with some combination of: TypeScript / JavaScript React / Next.js Node.js PostgreSQL Supabase or similar platforms SaaS architecture Multi-tenant applications Authentication and authorization APIs and third-party integrations Payments/subscriptions Cloud infrastructure Security Testing and CI/CD AI-assisted software development Experience building a SaaS product from 0 → production → real users is much more interesting to me than simply having a long list of technologies on your résumé. Bonus if you've previously: Built your own startup Been a founding engineer Built B2B SaaS Worked on vertical SaaS Worked with scheduling/booking systems Built multi-location or multi-tenant products Spoken directly with SaaS customers Managed or mentored engineers What I Don't Care Much About I don't care much about: Fancy titles Big-company logos Perfect degrees Whether you went to a famous university Whether your résumé looks impressive I'd rather meet someone who has quietly built three excellent products than someone who spent years in meetings at a famous company. Show me what you've built. Probably Not a Fit If… You're looking for an immediate salary. You see this mainly as a side freelance project. You only want to receive tickets and write code. You don't like talking to customers. You need every requirement fully documented before starting. You aren't comfortable with uncertainty. You want a CTO title but don't want to be hands-on. Or you're mainly attracted by the word "co-founder" rather than the work required to build a company. Commitment I'm looking for someone interested in a serious, long-term founder relationship. I'm open-minded about whether we begin part-time or full-time depending on your current situation. What matters much more is consistency, ownership and our ability to gradually build Limespun together. If you only have a few random hours available occasionally, however, this probably isn't the right fit. About Me I'm an open-minded, friendly and product-focused founder. I care deeply about building products properly, understanding why we're building something, questioning assumptions and continuously improving. I don't want a formal founder relationship where we're afraid to disagree with each other. I'd rather build with someone where we can say: "I think you're wrong — here's why." Discuss it. Make the best decision. And move forward without ego. I want a co-founder relationship that is ambitious, transparent, calm and genuinely enjoyable. Building a startup is already difficult. The people you're building it with shouldn't make it harder. Why Limespun? Tattoo studios are fascinating businesses. They combine: Artists Appointments Customers Deposits Scheduling Multiple employees Studio operations Inventory Communication Compliance Customer experience Repeat business Multiple locations Business analytics Yet many studios still operate across fragmented tools, manual workflows and generic software that wasn't designed around how tattoo studios actually work. We believe there's an opportunity to build a deeply vertical product that tattoo professionals genuinely love using every day. Our goal isn't to build another generic booking tool. We want Limespun to become the operating system for tattoo businesses. And if we execute well, the same foundation can create opportunities far beyond the initial market. How to Apply Please don't send me a generic AI-generated cover letter. I'd much rather receive a short, genuine message answering these: 1. What is the best product you've personally built? Send a link, GitHub, demo or screenshots if possible. 2. What part did you personally build? 3. Have you ever taken a product from idea to real production users? 4. Are you comfortable with an equity-only co-founder position at this stage? 5. Roughly how much time could you consistently commit? 6. What's your timezone/location? 7. Are you comfortable occasionally talking directly with customers in the US/UK? 8. Why does building a vertical SaaS company interest you? And finally: Tell me something you strongly disagree with about how most startups build software today. I'm particularly interested in that answer. If there's alignment, we'll start with conversations and some working sessions together before making any major commitment. I care much more about finding the right person than finding someone quickly. If you're technical, entrepreneurial, calm, curious and have been waiting for the right product to genuinely help build and own: I'd love to talk.

title: Senior Product QA Engineer - Manual
description: About Us Coursefinder.ai is the AI-powered study abroad platform built by KC Overseas Education — one of India's largest and most established overseas education groups. title: Software Engineer, Full Stack

Work closely with doctors, nutritionists, and strength coaches to translate clinical protocols into simple, intuitive software experiences. Design and implement AI/ML-powered features (e.g., predictive health scores, personalized habit nudges, progress tracking, real-time alerts). Take ownership of entire product verticals — from design discussions to production deployment — with speed and reliability. title: Data Scientist / Machine Learning Engineer (7-9 Years Experience)
description: RevOpt is building an AI-native Total Revenue & Profit Optimization System for the hospitality industry. The platform will help hotels move beyond siloed room pricing into coordinated optimization of demand, price, total revenue, and profit, with explainability and governance built in. We are looking for a hands-on Data Scientist / Machine Learning Engineer (3–5 years) to build the core intelligence layer: forecasting, demand and revenue modelling, pricing support, and decision signals that plug directly into our product. This is a build-and-ship role in a small team, working closely with the founders and our Backend Lead. What you’ll work on Design and implement forecasting models for demand, occupancy, ADR, revenue and other key KPIs using real hotel and market data. Build feature pipelines from PMS feeds, market intelligence, historical bookings, cancellations, and segments to create clean, model-ready datasets. Develop practical predictive and decision-support models that inform pricing, demand shaping and total revenue / profit optimization, rather than pure research models. Set up robust evaluation and back-testing frameworks to judge model quality on historic data before pilots. Collaborate with the Backend Lead to expose model outputs via services or scheduled pipelines that can be consumed by the RMS decision engine. Produce structured outputs and driver signals (e.g., pickup trends, comp-set shifts) that support explainable recommendations and AI-generated narratives. Participate in early pilot cycles, analysing results and refining models as we learn from real hotels. What you bring 3–5 years of applied ML / data science experience in product, SaaS, or analytics teams. Strong Python skills for data and modelling (pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn; bonus if you know Prophet, XGBoost/LightGBM, or ARIMA-style methods). Strong SQL and comfort working directly with relational data (PostgreSQL or similar). Hands-on experience with time-series / forecasting / demand / pricing / optimization problems (at least one serious project). Ability to take messy operational data, clean and structure it, engineer features, and build models that can be used in production. A product mindset: you care about commercial relevance, stability and explainability, not just marginal accuracy gains. Nice to have Experience with Airflow / Dagster / MLflow or similar tools for ML pipelines and experiment tracking. Exposure to pricing, revenue management, operations research, or decision-heavy domains (hospitality, travel, fintech, retail). Experience deploying models behind FastAPI / Flask or working closely with engineers to operationalise models. Some exposure to LLM-based summarisation or explainability is a plus, not a requirement. If you want to build a real AI-native product in hospitality, work closely with experienced founders and a strong backend lead, and own the model layer end-to-end, we’d like to hear from you. Please answer the following when applying: Describe a forecasting or predictive model you built. What problem were you solving, what data did you use, and how did you evaluate whether the model was good enough? Have you worked with time-series, demand, pricing, or operational forecasting data before? If yes, briefly explain the project and your role. What is your comfort level with Python, SQL, and deploying or operationalizing ML outputs for use in a product? Have you worked on messy real-world datasets with missing values, inconsistent mappings, or noisy operational data? Briefly describe one such situation and how you handled it. Are you comfortable working closely with backend/product teams in an early-stage startup where models need to be practical, interpretable, and production-usable?

etc.) for specific use cases Multi-Agent Systems: Experience building multi-agent systems or agent orchestration RAG Expertise: Strong understanding and implementation of RAG (Retrieval Augmented title: Junior DevOps Engineer
description: About the role We run production AI infrastructure that serves real clients, real-time, at scale. Voice calls that can't buffer. Context retrieval that can't lag. Who you are You're the kind of engineer who treats infrastructure like software. You don't just deploy services. You build systems that stay up, recover gracefully, and are easy for the rest of the team to operate. You've debugged production incidents, optimized cloud costs, hardened Linux servers, and know that reliability comes from good engineering, not luck. You care about security, automation, and making deployments so predictable that they're almost boring. What you will do You'll work directly with our infrastructure and engineering teams, with exposure to the CTO, on the production platform that powers enterprise AI systems. Design, maintain, and improve our AWS infrastructure across compute, networking, and Kubernetes. Build and own CI/CD pipelines using AWS CodePipeline and CodeBuild to ship production services safely and consistently. Manage production Kubernetes clusters (EKS), including deployments, node groups, autoscaling (HPA and Cluster Autoscaler), and workload reliability. Deploy and optimize GPU workloads across EKS and EC2 for AI inference and infrastructure services. Design secure networking using VPCs, IAM, ALBs, NLBs, VPNs, and private networking. Build and maintain observability pipelines with OpenTelemetry, Grafana Alloy, and Prometheus to ensure production visibility. Troubleshoot production incidents across Linux systems, Kubernetes, networking, and cloud infrastructure. Continuously improve reliability, security, and cloud efficiency while automating repetitive operational work. Collaborate closely with backend and AI engineers to make deployments boring. Boring is good. Boring means nothing broke. Must-haves Strong hands-on experience with AWS infrastructure, including VPC, IAM, EC2, Lambda, and EKS. Experience managing Kubernetes clusters, including deployments, node groups, Horizontal Pod Autoscaling (HPA), and node autoscaling. Experience deploying and operating Docker-based workloads in production. Familiarity with AWS CodePipeline and CodeBuild or comparable CI/CD platforms. Experience configuring Application Load Balancers (ALB) and Network Load Balancers (NLB). Experience setting up and managing secure VPN connectivity (WireGuard preferred). Experience with OpenTelemetry, Grafana Alloy, and Prometheus for monitoring and observability. Strong Linux administration skills, including user and permission management, SSH hardening, filesystem management, and performance monitoring. Excellent debugging and troubleshooting skills across infrastructure, networking, and distributed systems. A security-first and cost-aware engineering mindset. Nice-to-haves Experience running and optimizing GPU workloads in production. Experience managing Linux development environments, including machine images, configuration management, and remote development tooling. Experience self-hosting developer or infrastructure tools. Contributions to open-source projects or a GitHub profile that demonstrates infrastructure or DevOps work. About Alchemyst AI Alchemyst AI is building the context layer for the agentic web - a verifiable context engine that gives AI agents persistent memory, business data, and operational context so they stay accurate, reliable, and production-ready. We believe the world is moving toward Agent Era 2.0, where context matters more than prompts. Prompts can be auto-optimized; what can't be faked is deep, tractable, verifiable context. That's the thesis we've bet our entire company on. We're a team of ~10 today. This is the ground floor. description: Our first dedicated security hire. You will be an individual contributor building the function. Seekho is built on one simple belief: make learning fun and easy for everyone. We are India's #1 video edutainment platform, helping people learn real-world skills through short, expert-led videos across digital services, business, Spoken English, and much more. Founded in 2020 by IIT Kanpur alumni Rohit Choudhary, Keertay Agarwal and Yash Banwani, we are trusted by 4M+ paid subscribers and were ranked No. 2 in Google Play's Top Trending App 2025 list. Your Role: You'll own security across all of our products. With a large engineering team shipping daily, that means building secure defaults and tooling that scale rather than reviewing everything by hand — security that's automatic, continuous and owned. It's a high-ownership role with significant independence, and you'll succeed by partnering closely with engineering teams. Enforce server-side authorization; defend against account takeover, promo abuse, payment tampering, and content piracy. Secure our mobile and AI surfaces, and keep children's, health, and payment data least-privilege and audited. Make SAST, DAST, SCA and secret scanning default in CI/CD, and keep results trustworthy so engineers act on them. Own our cloud posture — VPCs, security groups, IAM, secrets management, and threat detection. Run vulnerability management — the VAPT cadence and a channel for outside researchers to report issues and see fixes through. Build security incident management end to end, detection to postmortem, against India's short breach-reporting clock. Build Seekho's security platform — the internal libraries and guardrails engineers build on. Requirements Must Have: 4+ years in security, with real depth in application and API security. You think in terms of how systems get exploited, not just vulnerability categories. You can explain an authorization flaw in unfamiliar code, and code in Python or Go to build tooling. Working knowledge of cloud security — IAM, secrets, network controls, and threat detection. You've found real vulnerabilities yourself — a bounty, a VAPT finding, a CVE, or in your own product. Practical incident management, detection through postmortem — you've worked a real incident, not just written the plan. You've owned security in-house for a shipping product, as the first or only security person. Bonus: India's data-protection landscape (DPDP, SPDI/IT Act) and comfort partnering with legal/DPO Payments and subscription fraud, RBI autopay and tokenization; Children's-data obligations and Play Families / Apple Kids compliance; AI/LLM application security Exposure to ISO 27001 or SOC 2. title: Product Manager
description: AI-Native Financial Accounting for International Freight Forwarding & Supply Chain Location: Ahmedabad · On-site CTC: ₹12–18 LPA + meaningful upside as Shipmnts scales Experience: 3 years of maturity in product thinking and building You'll build the AI workflows and the AI employee workforce that run financial accounting for international freight forwarding and supply chain. Not another dashboard on top of a ledger, an AI Native accounting product where agents do the work. Forwarders, CHAs, NVOs and 3PLs move money across borders, currencies, entities and tax regimes every single day; today an army of finance staff stitches it together by hand in spreadsheets and portals. Your job is to change that: identify the highest-impact, highest-frequency finance jobs across billing, receivables, payables, tax and close, and put AI coworkers on them that draft, reconcile, file and explain — so finance teams close faster, chase less, and trust every number. 🌱 Our Product Culture Deep user empathy, first-principles thinking, tight cross-functional collaboration. We take inspiration from Jobs To Be Done and Deconstructing Work Elements, and we embed ourselves in customers' daily operations to understand their world. Our development rhythm: Ground Research → Brainstorm with AI → Iterative AI Prototyping → Develop → A/B Testing → Deploy → Adoption → Iterate again. 🧭 What You'll Own Finance Cloud, end to-end — the financial accounting product and the AI workforce that operates it. From the earliest discovery signal to post-launch iteration, you are the single accountable person for its direction and outcomes. You don't need to be a chartered accountant, but you must respect what a clean close and a correct invoice mean to the people who depend on them — and you'll build genuine accounting fluency fast. The problem space you'll shape: Agentic workflows — hunt across finance and adjacent departments for the high-impact, high-frequency tasks, map their real process and flows end to end, and automate them with agents. The unit of shipping isn't a feature; it's a job that no longer needs a human in the loop. The AI employee workforce — identify the roles a finance team fills today (AR clerk, AP executive, reconciliation analyst, tax preparer, collections agent) and build the AI coworkers that do that work reliably, with the right autonomy tiers and human-in-the-loop checkpoints where correctness is non-negotiable. Automated Invoicing Engine — freight sales invoices, credit notes and multi-leg charges, plus the billing engines beneath them: Detention, Demurrage & Storage automation, slab-window logic, late-milestone penalties, and the many-to-one surcharge relationships that today live in spreadsheets — all generated correctly, automatically, at scale. Global e-invoicing & taxation layer — jurisdiction-specific tax logic (GST, SST, VAT, withholding, reverse-charge, self-billing), field-level mapping to statutory e-invoice schemas (India IRN/GST, Malaysia MyInvois, and the next country we enter), across multiple companies, countries and currencies with entity-scoped books and consolidated reporting that still ties out. "The tax law changed" is a first-class roadmap input. Connected banking — embed an enterprise banking layer directly into the product: direct bank integrations, Bharat BillPay, payment gateways, and international payment providers, so money moves and reconciles without leaving Finance Cloud. AR automation with AI — ageing, statements, intelligent dunning, dispute handling and cash application, with agents that predict, prioritise and act on collections instead of finance chasing blindly. AP automation with AI — vendor bill capture, three-way matching against what was actually operated, exception handling and settlement — agents that clear the payables queue and flag only what needs a human. Reporting & insight for CFOs — the numbers a finance leader actually decides on, built on one report = one node, saved views nest beneath it, surfaced as insight rather than raw tables. Auditing & close layer — a faster, more trustworthy month-end: automated reconciliations, audit trails, flux analysis and the controls auditors expect, compressing the close from weeks to days. 🔍 Discovery & Domain Depth Develop genuine operational and accounting expertise — not just user interviews, but workflow shadowing with AR/AP teams, controllers and CFOs, support mining, and cohort-level behavioural analysis. Translate complex accounting workflows, tax rules, and compliance requirements into sharp problem frames: the underlying job to be done and the exact friction blocking it. Maintain a live insight repository that feeds roadmap decisions continuously. 🗺️ Roadmapping & Prioritization Own the multi-quarter Finance Cloud roadmap — balancing near-term delivery, mid-term bets (new agents, new-country compliance), and platform investments in the underlying ledger and data model. Prioritize using RICE, opportunity sizing, and sharp judgment — and defend your calls to leadership with clarity, including where regulatory deadlines override everything else. Document deprioritization explicitly; the roadmap is only credible when stakeholders understand what's not on it and why. 🤖 AI Prototyping Rapidly prototype multiple solution directions using AI-assisted tools before committing engineering capacity. Run timeboxed prototype sprints, surface trade-offs across competing approaches, and treat every prototype as a learning instrument — not a deliverable. 🔪 Deciding What to Build and What to Kill Design eval frameworks across user comprehension, task completion, correctness, and business value — for finance features, correctness is non-negotiable and belongs in every rubric. Score prototypes on a clear rubric, run usability sessions with real finance users, and make the call — with explicit rationale and conviction. ⚙️ Shaping, Speccing & Building Connect domain experts, CFO-level buyers and ground users' insights into unambiguous, engineer-ready specs: flows, edge cases, state definitions, tax and rounding rules, data contracts, and acceptance criteria. Be especially rigorous on the details that break real books — currency conversion, tax treatment, reversal/credit-note flows, audit trails, and approval workflows. Own sprint planning, scope decisions, and delivery accountability; know when cutting scope cuts value, and when it quietly breaks compliance. 🚀 Launching & Iterative Adoption Coordinate cross-functional launches and track adoption cohorts week-over-week post-release. Partner with CS and Implementation on migration and data integrity — finance features have no tolerance for silent data loss. Run structured retrospectives after every major launch — not for compliance, but to get sharper. 📈 Growth & GTM Motion Define the north star and health metrics for Finance Cloud, own activation/adoption/retention, and design structured experiments with clear hypotheses, instrumented from day one. Think through pricing and packaging for every major feature — base plan, tier uplift, usage-based, or outcome-based (e.g., automation that recovers demurrage the customer would otherwise eat). Write launch briefs that arm Sales and CS with positioning, FAQs, and objection handling, and define launch success upfront: adoption curve, revenue contribution, support deflection, and NPS signal. ✅ What You'll Bring Experience that shows more than 3 years of maturing in product thinking and building — a track record of end-to-end ownership and measurable outcomes, not just tenure. Having worked on B2B enterprise SaaS is a strong plus. Wrangle with data to generate insights and uncover patterns: comfortable with SQL, dashboard interpretation, and experiment design without needing an analyst. Fluent with the AI tool stack — prototyping, spec writing, and research acceleration in your everyday workflow. A strong background in financial accounting — prior experience in a fintech product, Big 4, or a CA with a product mindset — will give you a strong edge. 🧠 Who You Are You think in systems but execute in specifics. A storyteller who can communicate visually, verbally and in writing — simplifying the complexities of financial accounting so every team gets it. A product influencer who inspires and rallies everyone around them to crack the most complex problems — the ones that felt unsolvable. You hold strong opinions and update them when the evidence shifts. You sweat the details because you know that in finance, a rounding error isn't a rounding error. You're a sharp decision-maker who wants ownership, not just responsibility — and you know the difference. 🎁 What You'll Get Full ownership of a product cloud with real enterprise customers and real financial complexity. A direct seat at the strategic table with leadership. A team that values craft and depth over velocity theatre. Competitive comp (₹12–18 LPA) with meaningful upside as Shipmnts scales.

title: Founding Robotics Engineer, Simulation & Autonomy.
description: Read this first: We're hiring our founding robotics simulation engineer. You will spend your days in Gazebo and Isaac Sim, writing C++ and Python against ROS2, validating SLAM and motion planning for drones and AMRs. If you haven't built simulation environments for physical robots, this role is not for you. Fullstack, web, mobile, and general ML backgrounds will not be considered, regardless of how strong. About Grazen Grazen is a stealth-mode robotics startup building the AI brain for warehouse operations. We deploy autonomous drones and AMRs across warehouses and distribution centers, eliminating manual counts, catching stock discrepancies in real time, and delivering audit-grade inventory intelligence every day. Hardware-agnostic, cloud-native, already in paid pilots. Join a hands-on founding team shaping the future of autonomy for industry. The Role You'll own Grazen's simulation and autonomy pipeline. Every drone and AMR that flies or drives at a customer site runs code you've validated in sim first. A counterpart founding engineer owns the warehouse-floor side: live deployments, customer-site bring-ups, field debugging. You own the playground they ship from, and the autonomy stack that runs on the fleet. What You'll Do Build and maintain sim environments in Gazebo and Isaac Sim that mirror real warehouses. Racking geometry, aisle widths, lighting, SKU density, clutter. Procedurally generate warehouse variants for domain randomization. Different layouts, different rack heights, different lighting conditions, different drone and AMR models on the same stack. Own the nav and planning stack: motion planning, behavior trees, obstacle avoidance, GPS-denied flight trajectories through multi-height racked aisles. Replay field logs from customer deployments as regression tests. When something breaks at a customer site, your harness reproduces it in sim within the hour. Generate synthetic training data for the ML team's perception models. Barcode views at odd angles, poor lighting, partial occlusion, damaged packaging. Build the CI pipeline for autonomy. Every PR from the SF engineer runs against a sim suite before it touches a real drone. Validate new drone and AMR hardware in sim before first field flight. New sensor payload, new compute module, new airframe: it flies in sim first. Debug SLAM failures by replaying field data. Figure out what broke, fix it in the stack, validate the fix held across the full regression suite. Technical Skills Strong in C++ and Python (ROS2). Hands-on with Gazebo, Isaac Sim/Isaac Gym, or equivalent robotics simulators. Nav stacks, motion planning, SLAM. You've shipped autonomy code that ran on real hardware, not just in a paper. Comfortable building reproducible test harnesses and CI pipelines for robotics code. Synthetic data generation and domain randomization techniques for perception training. Bonus: warehouse, inspection, or industrial drone/AMR background. Experience with sim-to-real transfer. RL frameworks (Stable Baselines3, Isaac Gym). Photorealistic rendering pipelines (Omniverse, Unreal). GitHub or portfolio showing real-world robots you've shipped. Who You Are Systems thinker. You care that the sim matches reality tightly enough that the SF engineer trusts it. Independent builder. Comfortable being the robotics anchor in India while working closely with the SF counterpart across timezones. Strong communicator. You write clean issue reports, document your sim environments, and translate between the SF robotics engineer and the ML team without noise. Prior startup, research, or small-team experience strongly preferred. Qualifications BS/MS/PhD in Robotics, CS, EE, or related. 4+ years hands-on robotics experience with deployed systems (drones or AMRs). Based in Bengaluru or Hyderabad. This role is in-office. Not remote. What Grazen Offers Founding engineer seat with meaningful equity. Early customer traction. Your sim work gates live customer deployments within your first 30 days. Direct collaboration with the founding team and the SF robotics counterpart. Opportunity to shape product and company DNA at the earliest stage.

title: AI/ML Engineering Intern - Marvedge
description: About Marvedge Marvedge is a SaaS video product for creating interactive, trackable product demos - screen recordings with branding, watermarking, Al voiceover, subtitles, CTAs, and shareable QR codes, used by SaaS teams to convert prospects. We're now building V3: an engine that takes a customer's long-form video (webinars, product tours, podcasts) and automatically repurposes it into short, vertical, Al-voiced clips with embedded lead capture - turning passive content into a distribution and pipeline channel. You'd be joining pre-team - there is no existing dev org yet. You will be one of the first engineers building this from scratch, working directly with the CTO. What you'll actually build This is not a research role. The job is to get real AI/ML capability shipped into a production Next.js/TypeScript app in weeks, not months - which means integrating and orchestrating existing models and hosted-inference APIs, not training models from scratch or vendoring unmaintained academic repos. Concretely, you will own: • Transcription & virality scoring - run long-form source video through Whisper (word-level timestamps) and build an LLM-based scoring chain (OpenAl) that ranks candidate 15—60s segments by "viral potential," producing hook titles and start/end timestamps. (You'll be extending a pattern that already exists in our codebase for Al script tone-rewriting - you'll study and reuse it, not invent it from zero.) • Vertical reframing pipeline - integrate hosted inference for face/saliency detection and active-speaker detection (via vendor APIs such as Sieve/Replicate-style hosted models, not by trying to build/train MediaPipe AutoFlip or TalkNet-ASD in-house - both are unmaintained/academic and out of scope for our timeline) to drive 16:9 9:16 cropping and dual-speaker split-screen logic. • Kinetic subtitle generation - generate Advanced SubStation Alpha ( . ass ) caption files with word-level karaoke highlighting, burned in via ffmpeg/libass. We already burn stabilized captions for another feature; you'll extend that approach for short-form. • Al dubbing pipeline - integrate the Elevenl_abs Dubbing API (translation + voice cloning) for multi-lingual shorts, and reuse/adapt our existing audio-visual pacing-alignment logic (time- stretch vs. freeze-frame padding) that keeps dubbed audio in sync with video. • Pipeline orchestration - wire all of the above into background jobs (queue-based, on our existing Cloud Run/Node worker), with clear stage-by-stage state so failures at any step degrade gracefully instead of breaking the whole export. What we need from you Must-have • Strong Python fundamentals - comfortable writing production-quality (not notebook-only) code. • Working knowledge Of how modern ML APIs are consumed in practice: REST/API integration, handling async jobs, webhooks, polling, rate limits, retries. • Basic understanding of audio/video concepts: frames, timestamps, sample rate, codecs - you don't need to be a video engineer, but you shouldn't be starting from zero. • Comfortable reading model/APl docs and being the person who evaluates "does this vendor's output quality actually work for our use case," not just "does the API call succeed." • Currently in 3rd or 4th year Of a CS/related degree. Strongly preferred • Exposure to ffmpeg (even basic CLI usage - trimming, cropping, concatenation). • Familiarity with any of: Whisper/speech-to-text APIs, TTS APIs (ElevenLabs, Deepgram, etc.), computer vision basics (face detection, OpenCV). • Some exposure to LLM prompting/chains (OpenA API, LangChain or similar) - you'll be designing prompts that produce structured, reliable output (e.g., scored clip segments as JSON), not freeform chat. • Any past project (hackathon, coursework, personal) involving video/audio processing or applied ML - even a rough one. We care more about a working demo than a polished GitHub README. Good fit if you • Prefer "ship a working VI with a hosted APP' over "spend three weeks trying to get an academic repo to run." • Are comfortable with ambiguity - specs will be directional, not exhaustive, and you'll be expected to flag when something in a plan isn't actually feasible in the timeline rather than silently struggling with it. • Want ownership: as an early intern here, code you write in your first month can plausibly still be running in production in six. • Can communicate technical trade-offs clearly (e.g., "this vendor is cheaper but adds 2s Of latency per clip") - you'll be making some Of these calls, not just executing a spec. What this role is explicitly NOT • Not a "build a novel active-speaker-detection model" research role. We buy or wrap that capability; we don't build it in-house at this stage. • Not a data science/analytics role - no dashboards-and-Jupyter work. • Not purely backend - you'll write integration code, not deep infra, though you'll collaborate closely with whoever owns the backend/queue layer

title: Founding Engineer - Equity-Only Compensation (Up to 10% Equity + 20% of Profit)
description: ⚠️ EQUITY-ONLY COMPENSATION There is no salary. Not a reduced salary - none. You are paid in ownership: up to 10% equity and up to 20% of monthly profit, paid out every month. If that doesn't work for your situation, please stop reading here. No hard feelings and no wasted time on either side. There is a working product. There is no interface. That's the job. Point Seen in Search at a domain and, in about forty seconds, it asks ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google AI Overviews what they actually say about that company, parses the verbatim answers, and scores the result deterministically. A real scan of stripe.com came back 80/100 - "Category Leader" - in 42 seconds across all three engines. Nobody can see any of it. The pipeline is a library and a queue worker. There is no first page, no scorecard, no export, no deploy pipeline. You would build all of it. About Seen in Search Every company spent twenty years learning to rank on Google. Now their buyers ask an AI instead, and most of them have no idea what it says back. Seen in Search answers that — and then fixes it. Not a checker. Not an advisor. An executor. Scan → Execute → Verify. On-page and technical work gets executed for the customer; off-site citation work is assisted. One rule shapes the whole product: we publish observations, not verdicts. Every claim carries its engine, its exact question, and its UTC date. "We asked ChatGPT X on 2026-07-16; here is its verbatim answer." Defensible forever. It's also a real design constraint - you'll feel it on every screen you build. Billed under FactoryJet Private Limited (India). Where things honestly stand Solo founder. No outside capital. No investors to answer to, and no runway from anyone else either. Pre-revenue. Zero customers today, which means zero profit share today. The engine works and is tested. Normalized Postgres schema, pg-boss queue and worker, a daily spend cap, 78 offline tests, verified against live engines. The marketing site is live. Next.js on Cloudflare Workers, auto-deploying. Everything between those two things is unbuilt. That's roughly six months of work, and it's yours. The deal - read this part twice No salary. Two forms of ownership instead. Equity - up to 10%. Four-year vest, one-year cliff. Real shares, papered properly, not a handshake. Profit share - up to 20%, paid every month. Not deferred to an exit. Not held until some funding round. The month we make money, you get paid that month. How profit is calculated - the whole formula Profit = what customers paid us this month − what it cost to serve them this month. The costs that come out are only the direct ones: AI engine and API costs (DataForSEO, Claude), servers and hosting, payment-gateway fees, software subscriptions, and any refunds. That's the list. No management fees, no allocated overhead, no invented line items. An example month (illustrative numbers, not a forecast): Collected from customers $10,000 − Expenses = $2000 = Profit $8,000 Your 20% share $1,600, paid that month You see the numbers. Every month, you get the same sheet I do - the revenue, the costs, the math. Nothing about your pay should ever be something you have to take on faith. Be clear-eyed about this: in a pre-revenue company, 20% of nothing is nothing. The profit share is genuinely uncapped and genuinely immediate, and it is also genuinely zero until we land customers. You need enough personal runway to survive the months before that happens. Please don't skip past this line. What you'll own The entire product surface. App shell, magic-link auth, the scan flow, live progress - the first screen a customer ever sees is one you design. Public scorecards at /score/, the methodology page, and OG images built to be screenshotted into a Slack channel and win the argument. Exports — Markdown, JSON, PDF — each one a publication that has to carry its own provenance. Ship and run it. Docker, Caddy, GitHub Actions, a Hetzner box. You deploy, you own the pager. Product calls. What gets built next, what gets cut, what the pricing is. You'll be in that conversation, not downstream of it. Your profit share means you have every reason to argue about pricing — good. Stack TypeScript · Next.js 16 · React 19 · Tailwind 4 · Prisma 7 + Postgres · pg-boss · Cloudflare Workers (OpenNext) · Docker + Caddy on Hetzner · DataForSEO · Claude. Strong opinions welcome. Nothing here is sacred except Postgres. What we're looking for Required You build with AI agents, seriously. Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Kimi — whatever you've made work. Not "I've tried Copilot." We're two people doing the work of eight, and this is how. Fundamentals underneath the agents. You can read what your agent just wrote and know it's wrong — the N+1, the missing index, the race in the worker, the test that passes for the wrong reason. Agents amplify judgment; they don't replace it. You design. This is a product that sells trust, and trust is transmitted almost entirely through the interface. Send a portfolio or live URLs. This is the hardest filter and the one I'll weigh most. You've shipped to production and kept it up. Containers, a reverse proxy, CI/CD, a Linux box you're not afraid of. Product instinct. You've killed a feature you liked because the evidence said to. Personal runway to cover the months before revenue starts, and clear eyes about the risk. Preferred SEO, search, or martech background - you'll get the customer faster Worked on something where correctness was a selling point Shipped a product solo, start to finish, however small Not a fit if You want a spec handed to you. You need a team around you. You'd describe design as "not really my thing." Or you're looking for a side project - this is not a nights-and-weekends role. How to apply Message me on Wellfound with: Something you designed and built - URL preferred over a résumé. How you actually use AI agents. What's in your setup, and one specific thing you've caught them getting wrong. One sentence on what you'd change about seeninsearch.com after looking at it. I read every message and reply to all of them. First conversation is 30 minutes, no prep.

You will work alongside AI teammates to handle merchant intelligence and custom workflows. This is an output-driven environment where leverage is the primary metric. Why This, Why Now Retail is undergoing a structural shift toward AI agents, and Swym is the layer that enables brands to capture intent. Our TSEs keep thousands of live storefronts humming while building the AI-leveraged support function of the future. title: Technical Account Manager - Marketing Analytics SaaS
description: Work directly with the growth and analytics teams at Uber, Delivery Hero, HelloFresh, Universal Music Group, and other category-defining global brands. About Clarisights Clarisights is a full-stack marketing analytics platform for humans and AI agents. We ingest data from every ad platform, analytics tool, and internal data source a marketer uses, model and harmonise it, and turn it into the dashboards and reports their teams run their business on. What you'll do You'll work hands-on with a small portfolio of large international customers. Your day-to-day: Run working sessions with your customers' analytics and marketing leads — understand their reporting needs and translate them into dashboards, calculated metrics, and data models inside Clarisights Investigate data questions that span SQL, our ingestion pipelines, and the customer's own sources ("why is this number different from what Meta Ads Manager shows?") Own the technical side of pilots and new customer onboarding — defining success criteria, building the initial reporting setup, and getting accounts to production-grade within the first few weeks Build and optimise reports and dashboards that hundreds of marketers inside our customer accounts use daily Translate customer requests into clear technical specs for our Product and Engineering teams, and help prioritise what gets built Spot expansion opportunities within customer organisations and feed them back to sales This isn't a ticket-queue support role. You own outcomes for your accounts and have direct relationships with senior stakeholders on the customer side. What you'll bring If you trained as an engineer but realised you'd rather solve problems alongside people than alone with an IDE, this role is for you. A degree in engineering 3–6 years in a technical, customer-facing role — Technical Account Management, Solutions Consulting, Implementation Consulting, Analytics Consulting, or similar Strong SQL and experience working with large, messy datasets Excellent written and verbal English — you'll be in daily contact with marketing and analytics teams across Europe and the US A first-principles problem-solver: when customers bring vague problems, your instinct is to ask sharp clarifying questions and guide the customer on the best approach Ability to explain technical concepts cleanly to non-technical stakeholders Nice to have Hands-on experience building reports or dashboards in at least one BI tool (Looker, Tableau, Metabase, Power BI, Mode, or similar) Background in performance marketing, growth, or marketing analytics — familiarity with platforms like Meta Ads, Google Ads, TikTok Ads, or MMPs (AppsFlyer, Adjust, Branch) Python or R for data analysis Exposure to data warehousing (BigQuery, Snowflake, Redshift) or ETL concepts What we offer Benefits like health insurance, meals at work, learning and conference budget…. Hybrid working from our Bengaluru office Direct exposure to some of the most sophisticated marketing teams in the world. The technical and commercial learning curve here is steep and durable — people who do this role for two years can go almost anywhere in SaaS or analytics next. Hiring process Our process takes 2–3 weeks end to end: Recruiter conversation (15 min) — we walk you through the opportunity and learn about your background Culture Fit Interview - ( 30 mins ) - we will outline the opportunity, review your work experience, and look for signs and evidence of culture fit. Customer Success team interview — ( 45-60 mins ) technical conversation focused on data analysis and problem-solving Take-home assignment — a realistic data + presentation exercise; you'll get a short briefing call with a peer, and we expect submissions back within a week Assignment presentation (60–90 min) — present and discuss your work with the team Founder conversation — meet at least one of our founders Offer — close on comp and start date with our talent team Clarisights is an equal-opportunity employer. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are committed to building a team that reflects the diversity of the customers we serve.

title: IT SaaS Solutions Consultant
description: Grovyn is looking for an experienced IT SaaS Solutions Consultant to help us identify and bring qualified technology projects to our delivery team. This is a relationship-led, performance-based commercial role for someone who already has meaningful relationships across IT, SaaS, software, consulting, technology services, or business transformation. This is not a traditional sales or lead-generation role. We are not looking for someone to cold call, scrape leads, or work from a database. We are looking for someone who already knows the market, has built trust with decision-makers, and can turn those relationships into real technology opportunities. What You'll Do You will work with the Grovyn team to identify, qualify, introduce, and help develop technology opportunities within your existing professional network, including: Identifying genuine IT, SaaS, AI, software, automation, and digital transformation opportunities Making warm introductions to founders, CEOs, CTOs, CIOs, business owners, procurement leaders, and other decision-makers Understanding the client's business problem and context before introducing Grovyn Helping us identify whether an opportunity has genuine business need, budget, and intent Participating in discovery conversations where your relationship or industry knowledge adds value Helping navigate the client relationship and buying process Supporting commercial conversations and opportunity development where appropriate Identifying additional opportunities within accounts and relationships you introduce Building long-term commercial relationships rather than simply passing one-off leads You do not need to be an engineer. You do not need to manage our developers. You do not need to manage project delivery. Grovyn's team handles discovery, solutioning, AI, architecture, engineering, delivery, and technical execution. Your advantage should be your relationships, credibility, market knowledge, and ability to open the right doors. What We're Looking For We are looking for someone with proven experience and an existing professional network, not someone trying to learn B2B technology sales from scratch. Required: 5+ years of experience in IT, SaaS, software, technology consulting, IT services, enterprise technology, or a closely related B2B technology environment Existing relationships with companies, founders, executives, technology leaders, or business decision-makers Strong understanding of how businesses evaluate and purchase technology Ability to identify genuine technology requirements within your network Strong understanding of B2B SaaS, IT services, software, AI, automation, or digital transformation Ability to make credible warm introductions Strong communication and relationship-management skills Commercial judgment and the ability to qualify opportunities Ability to work independently without a traditional sales-management structure Comfort with performance-based compensation Strong Fit If You Are You may be particularly well suited for this role if you are: An experienced IT consultant A SaaS consultant or advisor An independent technology consultant A former IT services or SaaS sales leader A technology partnerships professional An enterprise software salesperson A system integrator A digital transformation consultant A fractional technology advisor A business development professional with a strong technology network Someone who regularly receives technology requirements from existing clients or professional contacts Your job title matters less to us than the quality of relationships you can actually activate. The Network Matters More Than the Contact List We care about access and trust, not vanity metrics. If a CTO, founder, business owner, or technology leader would genuinely take your call and listen when you make an introduction, that is valuable to us. What Grovyn Can Deliver When you identify a genuine opportunity, you are not expected to build or deliver the solution yourself. Grovyn can support the opportunity across: Business and technical discovery Solution consulting AI strategy and implementation AI agents and intelligent workflows SaaS product development Custom software development Business operating systems CRM and ERP solutions Enterprise applications Cloud and system integrations Digital transformation Product engineering Technical architecture Implementation and delivery Long-term product and technology support The idea is simple: You bring the relationship and the opportunity. We bring the technology and execution. Compensation This is intentionally a performance-based, commission-only engagement. There is no fixed salary, monthly stipend, or guaranteed compensation associated with this role. We want to be completely transparent about that upfront. If you are specifically looking for a fixed-salary position, please do not apply. This opportunity is designed for experienced professionals who already have valuable relationships and want to create meaningful upside from those relationships. You will earn a minimum 10% revenue share on successfully closed business that you originate, irrespective of deal size. For example, if you originate and help close a $10,000 project, your minimum revenue share would be $1,000. If you originate a $50,000 project, your minimum revenue share would be $5,000. The upside scales with the business you help create. For larger or strategically important engagements, we are open to discussing the commercial structure based on the opportunity and your involvement. There are no arbitrary daily call targets. No requirement to send hundreds of cold emails. No requirement to work through scraped lead lists. We care about qualified opportunities and closed business, not activity for the sake of activity. Why This Could Be Interesting You may have spent years building relationships across your industry. People may already come to you when they have a technology problem. A former client may ask: > "Do you know anyone who can build this?" A founder may say: > "We need to automate this." A CTO may say: > "We need a partner who can actually execute this." A system integrator may need an engineering team behind them. You may know about these opportunities, but you may not have the engineering organization required to execute them. That's where Grovyn comes in. You don't need to build your own IT services company. You don't need to hire developers. You don't need to build an engineering team. You can bring the right opportunity to Grovyn, and our team can help turn it into a real engagement. Your network becomes the door. Grovyn becomes the execution engine. This Is Not For Everyone Please do not apply if you are: Looking for a fixed monthly salary Looking for guaranteed income A fresher trying to enter B2B sales Primarily a cold caller or lead-generation executive Looking for a company-provided database of prospects Expecting daily sales targets and structured sales management Uncomfortable with commission-only compensation Without an established professional network Looking for a conventional salaried sales position We would rather make that clear now than waste your time. Hands-On Commercial Experience Matters We want to understand what you have actually done, not just what your CV says. During the selection process, we may want to understand: Which industries and companies you have relationships with The types of decision-makers you can reach Technology projects you have personally influenced or introduced The approximate size of opportunities you have worked on How those opportunities originated Your role in the sales or consulting process The geographies where you have the strongest network The types of IT, SaaS, AI, software, or transformation projects you can realistically identify You do not need to disclose confidential client information. We simply want to understand whether your network can realistically create opportunities. What Would Make Us Excited About You We would get particularly interested if you can tell us something like: "I have strong relationships with manufacturing companies across India." "I regularly work with CTOs and CIOs across the GCC." "My previous enterprise clients still come to me for technology advice." "I know companies that regularly outsource software development." "I work with businesses currently evaluating AI and automation." "I have relationships with system integrators that need an engineering partner." "I regularly hear about technology projects before they reach the market." You do not need thousands of contacts. We would rather have 10 people who trust you than 10,000 people who don't know you. Engagement Role: IT SaaS Solutions Consultant Engagement: Independent / Contract Location: Remote Experience: 5+ years relevant experience Compensation: Performance-based, minimum 10% revenue share on successfully closed business originated by you Fixed Salary: None Work Model: Flexible and relationship-driven This is intended to be a long-term commercial relationship for the right person, not a short-term lead-generation assignment. How to Apply Please include the following in your application: Years of experience in IT, SaaS, software, consulting, or technology services Your current or most recent role Industries where you have the strongest relationships Countries or regions where you have the strongest network Typical decision-makers you can directly reach One example of a technology project or deal that came through your network Approximate deal size of that project, where you can disclose it Your specific role in originating or influencing the opportunity Approximate number of companies you could realistically introduce to Grovyn Types of IT, SaaS, AI, software, automation, or digital transformation projects you believe you could bring Your availability Confirmation that you are comfortable with a commission-only model with a minimum 10% revenue share and no fixed salary The Simple Version You have the relationships. We have the technology. The client has the problem. Together, we create the project. And when the project closes, you participate in the revenue you helped create. Minimum 10% revenue share. No fixed salary. No artificial activity targets. No cold-call quotas. No ceiling based on hours worked. Just real relationships, real opportunities, real execution, and real upside. If you already know where good IT and SaaS projects come from, we'd like to talk.

Our ambition isn't just to launch another app. Our ambition is to build transportation infrastructure that cities rely on. title: Creative & Automation Intern

Help shape our content format: the opening seconds, the reveal, the on-screen text, the end card. Run the existing Python + ffmpeg pipeline on each batch of footage, and review the output for quality — crops locked, overlays aligned, cuts landing on the beat. title: Outbound Sales Representative
description: What we do Raga connects boutiques and independent designers in North America, Europe, and Australia with Indian artisan craft networks. A designer in Copenhagen wants a run of Ajrakh block-printed linen. A boutique in Toronto wants white-label Phulkari pieces with their label on it. A brand in Melbourne wants custom fabric with specifications their mill can't touch. They come to us. We make it happen — through a decentralized network of artisan clusters across India. Everything is made-to-order. No dead inventory. Each order is a conversation — swatches, specifications, sampling, production. The founder manages all of that. What we don't have time for is finding the right people to have that conversation with. That's where you come in. Honest context We're early. There's no sales playbook, no SDR team, no hand-holding. This role starts as a short term contract — a 3-month period where we figure out if we're a good fit for each other. If you are, it converts to a longer term contract engagement with expanded scope and compensation. We'll make that criteria clear from day one so there's no ambiguity about what conversion looks like. The founder works full-time elsewhere and manages Raga on the side — which means once you open a door, they'll walk through it. Your job is to find the right doors. If you like figuring things out rather than following a script, this is that kind of job. What you'll actually do Find the right people Research and build prospect lists of boutiques, emerging designers, and small fashion brands across NA, Europe, and Australia. Not spray-and-pray — the right 50 over the wrong 500. Reach out and follow up Cold email, LinkedIn, Instagram DMs — whatever works. Write outreach that doesn't sound like outreach. Follow up without being annoying. That's the whole art of it. Have the first conversation When someone's interested, you don't immediately bounce them to the founder. You handle the initial exchange — what are they looking for, what's their timeline, what craft traditions interest them. Your textile background means you can speak their language. Once it's warm and qualified, you hand off. Automate everything you reasonably can if you're doing the same thing three times, build a system for it. Processes, lead enrichment, follow-up triggers — we want this machine to get smarter over time, not just bigger. If you spot something inefficient, fix it. Tell us what's working Weekly debrief with the founder. What messaging landed? What personas responded? What objections keep coming up? You're also our market research function. You might be a fit if You have a background in textiles — NID, NIFT, or just years of genuine obsession. You know what GSM means, what a warp is, and can tell an ikat from a jamdani. That knowledge is what lets you have a real first conversation with a designer, not just a booking call. You write well beyond emails. A blog post, a product description, a caption that made someone stop scrolling — you have work that shows you can tell a story in writing, not just communicate information. Share something you've written when you apply. You think like an engineer. When a process is broken or repetitive, your first instinct is to fix it — not complain about it. You've probably already automated something in your personal life that most people do manually. Your written English is excellent. Not just grammatically — you write with personality. The person on the other end should feel like a human wrote to them specifically, not an AI. You're comfortable with rejection and don't need constant validation to stay motivated. Cold outreach is mostly silence. You treat that as data, not discouragement. You're funny. Not performatively — just actually. We spend a lot of time working through ambiguous problems and life is too short to do that without a sense of humor about it. This is an internship to start — we care more about the right instincts than an impressive resume. Nice to have Experience with CRM or sales automation tools — Apollo, HubSpot, Lemlist, Instantly, Clay, whatever. Exposure to international fashion or design markets. You've used AI tools to do something useful, not just to generate text. Where this goes This short term contract runs for 3 months. If it's working — for both of us — it converts to a longer term contract role with broader ownership and better pay. In 6–12 months from there, as you learn the artisan network and the clients, the expectation is you own relationships end-to-end. We'll define what conversion looks like in writing during your first week. No vague promises.
